translations.text: …upon the name of the Lord.
And Abraham set out from there, and came, and camped in the wilderness.
And there was a famine in the land. And Abraham went down into Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine had grown severe in the land.
And it came to pass, when he drew near to Egypt, that Abraham said to his wife Sarah: "I know that you are a woman beautiful in appearance;
and when the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This is his wife,' and they will kill me, but they will receive you well.
Say, 'I am his sister,' so that it may go well with me because of you, and my life may be saved."
And it came to pass, when Abraham entered Egypt, that the Egyptians saw the woman, that she was very beautiful.
And Pharaoh's princes saw her and praised her before Pharaoh.
And they treated Abraham well on her account. And they brought Sarah into Pharaoh's house, and he had sheep and oxen and donkeys and male servants and female servants and mules and camels.
And God afflicted Pharaoh and all his house with great and grievous afflictions because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
Pharaoh called Abraham and said to him: "What is this that you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she is your wife?
Why did you say that she is your sister, so that I took her to myself as a wife? And now, here is your wife before you; take her and go."
And Pharaoh gave orders to his men concerning Abraham, that they should send him away, and his wife, and everything that was his, and Lot with him.
And Abraham came up out of Egypt, he and his wife and everything that was his, and Lot too with him, into the wilderness.
Abraham was very rich in livestock and in silver and in gold.
And he went back to where he had set out from, through the wilderness, as far as Bethel, as far as the place where his tent had been at first, between Bethel and Ai,
to the place of the altar which he had made there at first. And there he called upon the name of the Lord God.
And Lot, who had come along with Abraham, had sheep and oxen and tents.
And the land could not hold them, to dwell together, for their possessions were very great, and they were not able to dwell together.
And there was strife between the herdsmen of Abraham's livestock and the herdsmen of Lot's livestock. And the Canaanites were dwelling in that land.
Abraham said to Lot: "Let there be no strife between me and you, and between your herdsmen and mine, for we are kinsmen.
Is not the whole land here before you? Separate yourself from me: either you to the right and I to the left, or I to the right and you to the left."

And Lot lifted up his eyes and saw the whole region of the Jordan, that it was all well watered — before God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah — like the paradise of God and like the land of Egypt, as far as Zoar.
And Lot chose for himself the whole region of the Jordan. And Lot set out from the east, and they separated, each from his brother.
And Abraham dwelt in the land of Canaan, and Lot dwelt in the city of the region and settled in Sodom.
But the men of Sodom were very wicked and sinful before the Lord.
Then, after Lot had separated from him, God said to Abraham: "Lift up your eyes, and from the place where you are now, look to the north and the south, to the east and to the sea."
"All the land that you see I will give to you and to your descendants forever."
"And I will make your descendants like the sand of the earth. If anyone can count the sand of the earth, then your descendants can be counted too."
"Get up and walk through the land, through its length and its breadth, for I will give it to you."
So Abraham took up his tent and came and settled by the oak of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and there he built an altar to the Lord.
It happened in the reign of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Sillar [Ellasar], Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of the nations,
that they made war with Balak, king of the Sodomites, with Basa, king of the Gomorrahites, with Sinar king of Admah, with Sobomor king of Zeboiim, and with the king of Balak, that is, Zoar.
All these joined forces in the salt valley, that is, the Salt Sea.
For twelve years they had served Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer came, and the kings with him, and they slaughtered the giants who were in Ashteroth of Karan, and the strong nations, and the Emim in the city of Shaveh,
and the Horites in the mountains of Seir, as far as Belekun [?] of Paran, which is by the desert.
Then they turned back and came to the Spring of Judgment, that is, Kadesh. They slaughtered all the chiefs of Amalek, and the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.
The king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Balak, that is, Zoar, went out and drew up their lines to fight them in the salt valley,
against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of the nations, and Amraphel king of Salahar: these four kings against the five.
Now the salt valley was full of bitumen pits. The king of the Sodomites and the king of the Gomorrahites fled and fell into them, and the others fled to the mountains.
The enemy took all the horses of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food, and went away.
They also took Lot, Abraham's nephew, and his possessions, and went away, because he lived in Sodom.
One of those who had escaped came from there and told Abraham, who was living by the oak of Mamre, Olmor [?], the brother of Eshcol and the brother of Aner.
Abraham heard that his nephew Lot had been taken captive. He mustered the servants born in his own household, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them as far as Dan.
He attacked them by night, he and his servants, and struck them down. He chased them as far as Hobah, which is to the left of Damascus,
and he brought back all the horses of Sodom. He also brought back his nephew Lot and all his goods, and the women and the people.
The king of Sodom came out to meet Abraham when he had returned from slaughtering Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, in the valley of Shaveh, that is, the plain of the kings.
And Melchizedek, king of Salem, brought out bread and wine to Abraham. And he was a priest of God Most High.
And he blessed Abraham and said: Blessed is Abraham by God Most High, who created the heavens and the earth,
and blessed is God Most High, who has given your enemies into your hands. And Abraham gave him a tenth of everything.
The king of the Sodomites said to Abraham: Give me the men, and take the horses for yourself.
Abraham said to the king of the Sodomites: I stretch out my hands to God Most High, who created the heavens and the earth,
that I will not take anything of all that is yours, from a thread to a sandal-strap, to the fastenings, so that you may not say: I made Abraham rich,
except what these young men have eaten, and the share of these men who came with me: Eshcol, Aner, Mamre. Let these take a share.
After these words the word of the Lord came to Abraham and said: Do not be afraid, Abraham. I will help you, and your reward will be very great.
Abraham said: Lord, what will you give me? For look, I am left childless, and the son of Masek, my household servant, is this Eliezer of Damascus.
And Abraham said: For you have not given me offspring. This servant of my household will inherit from me.

And at once a voice came to him and said to him: That one will not be your heir. The one who comes out of you will be your heir. 5. And he brought him outside and said to him: Lift up your eyes to heaven and count the stars, if you are able to count them. And he said: So shall your offspring be. 6. And Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
And he said to him: I am God, who brought you out of the land of the Chaldeans to give you this land as an inheritance.
And Abraham said: Lord, Lord, how shall I know that I will inherit it?
And God said to him: Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove and a pigeon.
Abraham took all these and cut them in half down the middle, and he laid the halves out facing one another. But he did not divide the birds.
And birds came down on the divided flesh, and Abraham sat down with them.
And just as the sun was setting, a trance fell on Abraham, and suddenly a great dread of darkness came over him.
And he said to Abraham: Know for certain that your offspring will be foreigners in a land that is not their own, and they will enslave them and mistreat them for four hundred years.
But I will judge the nation that they serve, and after this they will come out here with many goods.
As for you, you will go to your fathers in peace, having been brought to a good old age.
And in the fourth generation they will return here, for the sins of the Amorites are not yet complete.
And when the sun was setting, there was a flame, and suddenly there was a smoking furnace and torches of fire, and they passed between the divided pieces.
On that day God made a covenant with Abraham and said: To your offspring I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates:
the Sinites [?] and the Kenizzites and the Kadmonites,
the Hittites and the Perizzites and the Rephaim
and the Sarelites [?] and the Canaanites and the Hivites and the Girgashites and the Jebusites.
But Sarah, his wife, bore him no children. She had an Egyptian maidservant whose name was Hagar.
In the land of Canaan Sarah said to Abraham: "Behold, God has kept me from bearing children. So go in to my maidservant, so that you may have children by her." And Abraham listened to Sarah's voice.
So Sarah, Abraham's wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her maidservant, after Abraham had lived ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abraham her husband to be his wife.
He went in to her, and she conceived. When she saw that she had conceived, her mistress became despised in her eyes.

Sarah said to Abraham: "I am wronged because of you. I gave my maidservant into your embrace. As soon as she saw that she had conceived, I became despised in her eyes. May the Lord judge between you and me."
Abraham said to Sarah: "Behold, your maidservant is in your hands. Do with her as you please." Then Sarah treated her harshly, and she fled from her presence.
The angel of the Lord found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, the spring on the road to Shur.
The angel of the Lord said to her: "Hagar, maidservant of Sarah, where are you coming from?" She said to him: "I am fleeing from the presence of Sarah, my mistress."
The angel of the Lord said to her: "Return to your mistress and humble yourself, humble yourself [?] under her hand."
The angel of the Lord said to her: "I will greatly multiply your offspring, so that they cannot be counted for their multitude."
The angel of the Lord said to her: "Behold, you are with child, and you will bear a son, and you shall call his name Ishmael, for the Lord has heard your humiliation."
"He will be a wild man. His hands will be against all, and the hands of all against him, and he will dwell in the presence of all his brothers."
And Hagar called upon the name of the Lord who had appeared to her: "You are the God who looked upon me." For she said: "I have seen face to face the one who appeared to me."
Therefore that well was called "the Well where I saw [him] before me"; behold, it is between Kadesh [?] and Bered.
Hagar bore Abraham a son, and Abraham called his son, whom Hagar bore to him, Ishmael.
Abraham was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael.
When Abraham was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to Abraham and said to him: "I am your God. Be pleasing before me and be blameless.
I will set my covenant between me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly."
Abraham fell on his face, and the Lord spoke with him and said:
"As for me, behold, I am making my covenant with you, and you will be the father of many nations.
No longer shall your name be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham, for I have made you the father of many nations.
I will make you exceedingly fruitful and make you into nations, and kings shall come forth from you.
I will establish my covenant between me and you and your offspring after you, throughout their generations, as an everlasting covenant, to be God to you and to your offspring after you.
I will give to you and to your offspring after you the land in which you are sojourning, all the land of Canaan, as an everlasting possession, and I will be their God."
And the Lord said to Abraham: "You shall keep my covenant, you and your descendants after you, throughout their generations."
"And this is the covenant that you shall keep between me and you and between your descendants after you, throughout their generations: you shall circumcise every male among you."
"And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin as a covenant between me and you."

"And you shall circumcise the child when he is eight days old, every male among you throughout your generations: the one born in your house, and the one bought with silver who is born of foreign stock and is not of your descendants."
"The one born in your house and the one bought with silver shall surely be circumcised. And my covenant shall be in your flesh as an everlasting covenant."
"And the male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be cut off from his people, for he has broken my covenant."
The Lord said to Abraham: "As for Sarah your wife, her name shall no longer be called Sarah; Sarra shall be her name."
"And I will bless her and give you a son by her, and I will bless him too. And she shall become a great nation, and kings of nations shall come forth from you."
And Abraham fell on his face and laughed in his heart and said: "Will a son be born to a man a hundred years old, and will Sarra, at ninety years old, give birth?"
Abraham said to God: "May this Ishmael live before you, O Lord."

God said to Abraham: "Yes, behold, Sarah will bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac. And I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant, and with his descendants after him."
"And as for Ishmael, behold, I have heard you: I will bless him and make him grow and multiply him greatly. He shall beget twelve nations, and I will make him a great nation."
"But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this same time in the next year."
And he finished speaking these words to him, and God went up from Abraham.

And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all those born in his house, and all those bought with silver, and every male among the men of Abraham's house, and he circumcised their foreskins at that very time on that same day, as God had told him.
Abraham was eighty-nine years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin,
and Ishmael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
At that very time on that same day Abraham was circumcised, and Ishmael his son.
And all the men of his house, both those born in the house and those bought with silver from foreign peoples, he circumcised.
God appeared to Abraham by the oak of Mamre, while he was sitting at the door of his tent at midday.
He raised his eyes and looked, and behold, three men were standing over him. And he saw them, and he rose and ran from the door of his tent to meet them, and he bowed down to them to the ground.
And he said to them: "My lords, if I have found favor in your sight, do not pass by your servant."
"Let water be brought and let them wash your feet, and rest in the shade under the tree."
"And let bread be brought, and eat, and after this go on your way, since you have turned aside to your servant." And they said: "Let us do as you have said."
And Abraham hurried into Sarah's tent and said to her: "Quickly, make ready three measures of fine flour, knead it, and make cakes."
And Abraham ran to the herd and took a calf, tender and good, and gave it to the servant, and he hurried to prepare it.
And he took butter and milk and the calf that he had prepared, and set them before them, and they ate. And he stood before them under the tree.
They said to Abraham: "Where is Sarah your wife?" He answered and said: "Look, there, in the house."
The Lord said to Abraham: "I will return and come to you at this same time next season, and Sarah will have a son."
Abraham and Sarah were old and advanced in days. The way of women had ceased for Sarah.
Sarah laughed in her heart and said: "This has never yet been granted to me until now, and now my lord is old."
The Lord said to Abraham: "Why did Sarah laugh in her heart and say, 'Shall I truly bear a child, when I have grown old?'
Is any word impossible with God? At this same time I will come to you, as you have desired, and Sarah will have a son."
Sarah denied it and said, "I did not laugh," for she was afraid. And he said to her: "No, you did laugh."
The men rose up from there and looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah. And Abraham went along with them, seeing them on their way.
And the Lord said: "Shall I hide from Abraham my servant what I intend to do?
Abraham shall become a great and numerous nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him.

For I know that he will command his children and his household after him, and they will keep the ways of the Lord, doing righteousness and justice, so that the Lord may bring upon Abraham everything that he spoke to him."
And the Lord said: "The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah has grown great, and their sins are great.
I will go down and see whether they are doing what the outcry against them that comes to me says, so that I may know."
And they turned from there and went to Sodom. But Abraham was still standing before the Lord.
And Abraham drew near and said to the Lord: "Will you destroy the righteous along with the ungodly, so that the righteous fare the same as the ungodly?
If there are fifty righteous people in that city, will you destroy them? Will you not spare that whole place for the sake of the fifty righteous, if they are in it?

Surely you will not act in this way, killing the righteous along with the ungodly, so that the righteous fare the same as the ungodly? Surely you who judge all the earth will not fail to do [?] justice?"
And God said: "If I find fifty righteous people in Sodom, I will spare that whole place for their sake."
Abraham answered and said to God: "I have now begun to speak to the Lord, though I am dust and ashes.
If the fifty righteous are five short, will you destroy the whole city because of those five?" And God said: "I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there."
And Abraham spoke again: "What if forty are found there?" And the Lord said: "I will not destroy it for the sake of the forty."
And Abraham said: "Do not be angry, Lord, if I speak further: what if thirty are found?" And he said: "I will not destroy it if I find thirty there."
And Abraham said: For I still have a word to say to the Lord: what if twenty are found there? And he said: I will not destroy it for the sake of the twenty.
And Abraham said: Do not be angry, Lord, if I speak just once more: what if ten are found there? And the Lord said: I will not destroy it for the sake of the ten.
And the Lord went up when he had finished speaking to Abraham. And Abraham went back to his own place.
The two angels came to Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting at the gates of the city. And when Lot saw them, he rose to meet them and bowed down with his face to the ground.
And he said: Look, my lords, turn aside to your servant's house and stay, and wash your feet; then rise early and go on your way. But they said: No, we will stay in the streets.
And he pressed them, and they turned aside to him and entered his house. And they prepared a supper for them and made them unleavened bread, and they ate, before they lay down to sleep.
But the men of the city, the Sodomites, surrounded the house, from the young to the old, all the people together.
They called out to Lot and said to him: Where are the men who came in to you tonight? Bring them out to us, so that we may lie with them.
Lot went out to them in front of the door, and the door was shut behind him.
And he said to them: By no means do this, brothers, and do not do evil.
I have two daughters who have not known a man. I will bring them out to you, and do with them as you please; only do nothing evil to these men, since they have come in under the roof of my house.

They said to him: Get out of the way! And they said: You came in here as a stranger, and not to act as a judge as well. Now we will do evil to you. And they pressed hard on the man, Lot, and came forward to break down the door.
The men inside stretched out their hands and pulled Lot into the house, and the doors of the house were shut.
And the men who were at the door were struck with blindness, from the small to the great, and they were scattered [?] and kept looking for a man to guide them [?].
The men said to Lot: Do you have anyone else here, sons or sons-in-law or daughters, or anyone else of yours in this city? Bring them out of this place,
for we are about to destroy this place, because the outcry against them has risen up before the Lord, and the Lord has sent us to destroy it.

Lot went out to tell his sons-in-law, who had taken his daughters as wives, and said to them: Get up and leave this place, for the Lord is destroying this city. But it seemed to them in their eyes that he was joking.

And when it was dawn, the angels urged Lot on and said to him: Get up and take out your wife and your daughters who are with you, and go out, so that you do not perish along with the lawlessness of this city.
And they were terrified, and the angels took his wife by the hand, and the hands of his two daughters, because the Lord was sparing them.
And they brought them outside and said: Save yourself, and do not look back, and do not stop anywhere in all this surrounding region. Flee to the mountain, so that you are not caught along with them.
Lot said to them: I beg you, my lords,
since your servant has found mercy in your sight, and you have shown me great mercy by saving my life: I cannot escape to the mountain, in case this evil overtakes me and I die.
Behold, this city is near enough for me to flee to. It is small, and I will be saved there, since it is small, and my soul will be saved through you.
And the Lord said to him: Behold, I have shown you favour in this matter too: I will not overturn this city that you spoke of.
Hurry, then, and escape there, for I cannot do the deed until you have entered it. For this reason the name of that city was called Segor.
The sun had spread over the city when Lot entered Segor.
And the Lord rained sulphur and fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah, from the Lord out of heaven.
And he overturned those cities and all the surrounding region, and all the inhabitants of that city, and every plant of the earth.
And Lot's wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
Abraham rose early at dawn and went to the place where he had stood before the Lord,
and he looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and toward all the land of the region, and he saw: behold, a flame of fire was going up from the earth like the smoke of a furnace.
And when the Lord destroyed the cities of the region, the Lord remembered Abraham and brought Lot out from the midst of the destruction, when the Lord overturned the cities in which Lot had lived.
Lot went up from Segor and settled on the mountain, and his two daughters with him, for he was afraid to live in Segor. And he lived in a cave, he and his two daughters with him.
The elder daughter said to the younger: Our father is old, and there is no one on earth who might come in to us, as is the custom of all the earth.
Come, let us give our father wine to drink and lie with him, and let us raise up offspring from our father.
And they gave him wine to drink that night [?]. And the elder went in and lay with her father that night, and Lot did not know when she lay down or when she rose.

And on the next day the elder said to the younger: Behold, I lay with our father yesterday. Let us give him wine to drink this night too, and you go in and lie with him, and let us raise up offspring from our father.
That night they gave their father wine to drink, and the younger went in and lay with her father, and he did not perceive when she lay down or when she rose.
And both of Lot's daughters conceived by their father.
And the elder bore a son and called his name Moab, saying: "From my father." He is the father of the Moabites to this day.
The younger also bore a son and called his name Ammon: "Son of my kin." He is the father of the Ammonites to this day.
And Abraham set out from there toward the land to the north, and he settled between Kadesh and Shur, and he sojourned in Gerar.

Abraham said of Sarah his wife: "She is my sister." He was afraid to say "She is my wife," in case the men of that city killed him because of her. Abimelech, king of the people of Gerar, sent and took Sarah.
God came to Abimelech in his sleep at night and said to him: Behold, you will die because of this woman, for she is joined to a husband.
But Abimelech had not touched her, and he said: Lord, will you destroy an ignorant and righteous nation?
Did he not say to me, "She is my sister," and did she not tell me, "He is my brother"? I did this with a pure heart and with righteousness of hands.
God said to him in the vision: "I know that you did this with a pure heart, and I held you back so that you would not sin against me. That is why I did not let you touch her."
This word was very hard in Abraham's eyes because of his son.

God said to Abraham: "Do not let it be hard in your eyes because of the boy and the maidservant. Whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for it is through Isaac that offspring shall be named for you.
But the son of that maidservant I will also make into a great nation, for he is your child."

Abraham rose at dawn, took bread and a skin of water, and gave them to Hagar. She put them on her shoulders, together with the boy, and he sent her away. She went off and wandered in the wilderness near the Well of the Oath.
The water in the skin ran out, and she left the boy under a shrub.
She went and sat down facing him at a distance, about a bowshot away, for she said: "Let me not see the death of my son." She sat facing him. The boy cried out and wept.

God heard the boy from the place where he was. The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her: "What is it, Hagar? Do not weep, for God has heard the voice of your boy from the place where he is.
Get up, bring your boy, and hold him by your hand, for I will make him into a great nation."
God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of living water. She went and gave the boy a drink.
God was with the boy. The boy grew up and lived in the wilderness, and he became an archer.
He settled in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother brought him a wife from the land of Egypt.
At that same time Abimelech, along with Ahuzzath, the steward of his household, and Phicol, the commander of his army, spoke to Abraham and said: "God is with you in everything you do.
Now swear to me that you will not harm me, or my descendants, or my house, but that you will deal with me and with the land where you are living according to the righteousness I have shown you."
Abraham said to him: "Yes, I will swear to you."
Abraham rebuked Abimelech over the wells of water that Abimelech's shepherds had taken from him.
Abimelech said to Abraham: "I do not know who did this. You did not tell me, and I did not hear of it until today."
Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant with each other.
Abraham set seven ewe lambs apart by themselves.
Abimelech said to Abraham: "What are these seven lambs of the flock that you have set apart by themselves?"
Abraham said: "Take [?] these seven lambs from me, so that they may be a witness for me that I dug this well."
For this reason the place was named the Well of the Oath, because there they swore an oath to each other.
They made a covenant at the Well of the Oath. Then Abimelech got up, with Ahuzzath the steward and Phicol, the commander of his army, and they went back to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham sowed a field by the Well of the Oath, and there he called on the name of the Lord God.
Abraham lived in the land of the Philistines for many days.
After these things, God tested Abraham and said to him, "Abraham, Abraham." And he said to him, "Here I am, Lord."
And he said to him, "Take your beloved son, whom you love, Isaac, and go to the high land, and offer him there as a sacrifice on one of the mountains that I will tell you of."

Abraham rose early in the morning and saddled his donkey. He took two servants with him, and Isaac his son, and he split wood for the sacrifice. He rose and went, and came to the place that God had told him of. On the third day
Abraham lifted up his eyes and saw the place from far off.
Abraham said to his servants, "Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there, and we will worship and come back to you."
He took the wood for the sacrifice and laid it on Isaac his son. He also took the fire and the knife, and the two of them went on together.
Isaac said to Abraham his father, "Father." And he said, "What is it, my son?" And he said, "Here are the fire and the wood. Where is the sheep for the sacrifice?"
Abraham said, "The Lord will see to the sheep for the sacrifice for himself, my son." And the two of them went on together.
They came to the place that God had told him of. Abraham built an altar to the Lord there and laid out the wood. He bound Isaac his son and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
And he stretched out his hand to take the sword and slaughter his son.
The angel of the Lord called to him from heaven and said, "Abraham, Abraham." And he said, "Here I am."
And he said, "Do not lay your hand on the boy, and do nothing at all to him. Now I know that you fear God, and you have not withheld your beloved son for my sake."
Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a ram was caught by its horns in a sabek bush. Abraham ran and took the ram and offered it as a sacrifice in place of Isaac his son.
Abraham named that place "The Lord saw," for to this day they say, "On the mountain the Lord appeared."
The angel of the Lord called to Abraham a second time and said to him,
"I swear by myself, says the Lord: because you have done this thing and have not withheld your beloved son for my sake,
I will surely bless you, and I will greatly multiply your offspring like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore. Your offspring will take possession of the cities of your enemies,
and all the nations of the earth will be blessed through you and through your offspring, because you obeyed my voice."
Abraham returned to his servants. They rose and went together to the Well of the Oath, and Abraham settled at the Well of the Oath.
After these things, Abraham was told: "Milcah too has borne sons to Nahor your brother:
Uz the firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of the Syrians,
Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel."
Bethuel became the father of Rebecca. These are the eight sons whom Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Taa [?], Tebah, Tahash, and Maacah.
Sarah lived one hundred and twenty-seven years.
And Sarah died in the city of Arbok, which is in the valley, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Abraham came to beat his breast for Sarah and to mourn her.
And Abraham rose up from beside his dead and said to the sons of Heth:
"I am a stranger and a sojourner among you. Give me a place for a grave among you, and I will bury my dead out of my sight."
The sons of Heth answered Abraham and said to him:
"Why so, lord? Hear us. You are a king from God. Bury your dead in the choicest of our graves. None of us will withhold his grave from you, so that you may bury your dead there."
Abraham rose up and bowed down to the people of that land, the sons of Heth.
He spoke to them and said: "If you truly wish me to bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and speak for me to Ephron, the son of Zohar,
and give me the double cave which is his, which is [?] on the side of his field. For as much silver as it is worth, give it to me among you as a possession for a burial place."
Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth. Ephron answered and spoke to Abraham before the sons of Heth and all who went in at the city, and said:
"Look to me, lord, and hear me: the field, and the cave that is in it, I give to you. Before all the citizens I give it to you, to bury your dead."
And Abraham bowed down before the people of that land.
And he said to Ephron in the hearing of all the people of the land: "Since you are on my side, hear me. Take from me the silver for the field, and I will bury my dead there."
Ephron answered Abraham and said to him:
"No, lord. For I have heard that it is worth four hundred shekel-weights. But what is that between you and me? Bury your dead."
And Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham gave him the silver that he had named in the hearing of the sons of Heth: four hundred shekel-weights of silver, tested by the merchants' standard.
And every tree that was in it, that is within its borders all around,
Abraham acquired before the sons of Heth and all who went in at the city.
After this Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the double cave of the field, which is opposite Mamre. This is Hebron, in the land of Canaan.
And the field and the cave were confirmed as Abraham's, as a possession for a burial place, by the sons of Heth.
Abraham was old and advanced in days, and the Lord had blessed Abraham in all things.
And Abraham said to his servant, the eldest of his household, who was in charge of everything he had: "Put your hand under my thigh,
and I will make you swear by the Lord, the God of heaven and earth, that you will not take a wife for my son Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell,
but that you will go to my own land, where I came from, to my land and my kindred, and take a wife for my son Isaac from there."
The servant said to him: "If the woman is not willing to come back with me to this land, shall I take your son back to the land from which you came out?"
Abraham said to him: "Take care that you do not take my son back there."

The Lord God brought me out of my father's house and from the land where I was born. He spoke to me, swore an oath to me and said: "To you I will give this land, and to your descendants." He himself will send an angel before you, and you shall bring a wife for my son from there.
If the woman does not want to come with you to this land, you will be free of this oath. Only do not take my son back there.
And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham, his lord, and swore an oath to him about this matter.
And the servant took ten of his lord's camels and some of all his lord's good things. He set out and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
And toward evening, at the time when the women who draw water come out, he made the camels kneel outside the city by the well of water,
and said: "O Lord, God of my lord Abraham, make my way prosper before me today, and show mercy to my lord Abraham.
Here I am, standing by this spring of water, and the daughters of the people who live in this city are coming out to draw water.

Let it be that the young woman to whom I say, 'Lower your pitcher so that I may drink,' and who says to me, 'Drink, and I will give your camels water too, until they are satisfied,' is the one you have prepared for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown mercy to my lord Abraham."
And before he had finished saying these words in his mind, Rebecca came out with a pitcher on her shoulder. She had been born to Bethuel, the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother.
The young woman was very beautiful in appearance. She was a virgin, and no man had known her. She went down to the well, filled the pitcher, and came back up.
Abraham's servant ran to meet her and said to her: "Give me a drink of water from your pitcher."
And she said: "Drink, my lord." She quickly lowered the pitcher onto her arms and gave him a drink.
And she said: "I will give your camels water too, until they have all drunk."
She quickly emptied the pitcher into the drinking trough, ran back to the well to draw water, filled it, and gave water to all the camels.
The man was watching her closely and kept silent, waiting to learn whether God had made his journey prosper or not.
When all the camels had finished drinking, the man took gold earrings weighing a shekel each and gold bracelets weighing ten drachmas each, and put them on her hands.
He asked her: "Whose daughter are you? Tell me whether there is room at your father's house for us to stay."
And she said to him: "I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son whom Milcah bore to Nahor."
And she said: "We have plenty of straw and fodder, and a place for you to stay."
The man was pleased. He bowed down to the Lord and said:
"Blessed is the Lord, God of my lord Abraham, who has not withheld his righteousness and his truth from my lord. The Lord has led me on the way to the house of my lord's brother."
And the girl ran to her mother's house and told her what had happened.
Rebecca had a brother named Laban. And Laban ran out to the spring.

Laban saw the earrings and the bracelets on his sister's hands, and he heard Rebecca's words as she told him, "This is what the man said." Then Laban came to the man while he was still standing at the spring.
And he said to him: "[?], come in. Blessed is God! Why do you stand outside? I have prepared the house for you, and a place for your camels."
And he brought him water to wash his feet, and the feet of the men who were with him.
And he set bread before them to eat. And the man said: "I will not eat bread until I have spoken my words." And they said to him: "Speak."
And he said: "I am Abraham's servant.
"And the Lord has greatly blessed my master, and he has become great. And he has sheep and cattle, silver and gold, male and female servants, and camels and donkeys in great number.
"And Sarah, his wife, bore my master one son in his old age, and he has given him everything that was his.
"And my master made me swear and said to me: 'You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell in their land,
"'but you shall go to my father's house and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son from there.'
"And I said to my master: 'What if the woman is not willing to come with me?'
"And he said: 'My Lord, before whom I have been pleasing, will send his angel before you and prosper your way, and you shall take a wife for my son from my kindred and from my father's house.
"'When you go to my kindred and they do not give her to you, then you will be free from my oath.'
"And today I came to this spring and said: 'O Lord God of my master Abraham! If you will prosper this way on which I am going,

"'see, I am standing now by this spring of water, and the daughters of the men of this city come out to draw water. Let it be that the maiden to whom I say, "Give me a little water to drink from your jar,"
"'and who says to me, "Drink, and I will water your camels too," she is the woman whom the Lord has prepared for his servant Isaac. And by this I will know your mercy toward my master Abraham.'

"And before I had finished saying these words in my mind, Rebecca came at once with a jar on her shoulders. And she went down to this spring and filled it. And I said to her: 'Give me a little water to drink.'
"And she quickly lowered the jar from her shoulder and said to me: 'Drink, and I will water your camels too.' And I drank, and she watered my camels too.
"I asked her and said: 'Whose daughter are you?' And she said: 'I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.' And I put earrings on her and bracelets on her hands.
"And I was glad, and I bowed down to the Lord and blessed the Lord God of my master Abraham, who has led me in the way of truth to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.
"Now if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me, so that I may turn to the right or to the left."
Bethuel and Laban answered and said: "This command has come from the Lord. Who is able to give you an answer [?] other than good?
"See, take her and go, and let her be the wife of your master, as the Lord God has said."
And when Abraham's servant heard these words of theirs, he bowed down to the Lord to the ground.
And Abraham's servant brought out vessels of gold and of silver and clothing and gave them to Rebecca. And he gave gifts to her brother and to her mother.
And they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and they slept. And the servant rose in the morning and said to them: "Send me away, so that I may go to my master."
Rebecca's brothers and her mother said to him: "Let this maiden stay with us a little longer, about ten days only, and after that you shall go."
And he said to them: "Do not hold me back, for the Lord has made my journey succeed. Send me away, and let me go to my master."
And they said to him: "Let us call the girl and ask her herself."
And they called Rebecca and said to her: "Will you go with this man?" And she said: "I will go."
And they sent away Rebecca their sister, with her dowry, and Abraham's servant and the men who were with him.
And they blessed Rebecca their sister and said to her: "You are our sister. Become thousands and tens of thousands, and may your descendants take possession of the cities of their enemies."
And Rebecca and her maidservants rose up, mounted the camels, and went with the man. And the servant took Rebecca and went away.
Now Isaac was walking in the field near the Well of the Vision, for he was living in the land to the north.
And Isaac had gone out into the field toward evening to take his ease. And he lifted up his eyes and saw camels coming.
And Rebecca lifted her eyes and saw Isaac, and she got down from the camel.
And she said to the servant: "Who is this man who is coming across the field to meet us?" And the servant said: "This is my master." And she took her garment and covered herself with it.
Then the servant told Isaac everything that he had done.
Isaac went into his mother's house and brought Rebecca in, and she became his wife. And Isaac was comforted for Sarah his mother.
Afterward Abraham took another wife, whose name was Keturah.
And she bore him Zimran and Jokshan, Medan and Midian, and Ishbak and Shuah.
And Jokshan fathered Sheba and Teman and Dedan. The sons of Dedan were Raguel, Nabdeel and Asshurim.
The sons of Midian were Ephah and Epher, Hanoch, Abida and Targa [?]. All these were the sons of Keturah.
Abraham gave all his possessions to Isaac his son.
And to the sons of his concubines Abraham gave gifts, and while he was still alive he sent them away from Isaac his son, toward the east.
These are the years of the days of Abraham's life, as long as he lived: one hundred and seventy-five years.
And Abraham died at a good old age, an old man and full of days, and he was gathered to his people.
And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the double cave, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, which is opposite Mamre.
That field and cave which Abraham had bought from the sons of Heth: there Abraham was buried, and Sarah his wife.
And after Abraham's death, God blessed his son Isaac. And Isaac settled near the Well of the Vision.
These are the generations of Ishmael son of Abraham, whom Hagar, Sarah's maidservant, bore to Abraham.
And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, according to the names of their generations: Ishmael's firstborn, Nebaioth; and Kedar, Adbeel, and Mibsam,
Mishma and Dumah, Massa,
and Hadad and Tema, and Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names in their tents and in their dwellings: twelve princes of their nations.
And these are the years of Ishmael's life: one hundred and thirty-seven years. And he died and was gathered to his people.
And he settled from Havilah as far as Shur, which is opposite Egypt, as far as where one comes toward the Assyrians. He settled facing all his brothers.
And these are the generations of Isaac, the son of Abraham: Abraham fathered Isaac.
And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Mesopotamia, the sister of Laban, as his wife.
Isaac prayed for Rebekah his wife, because she was barren. And God heard him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
And the children leapt in her womb, and she said: "If it is to be like this with me, why is this happening to me?" And she went to inquire of the Lord.
The Lord said to her: "Behold, two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall come out of your womb. And one people shall surpass the other people, and the elder shall serve the younger."
And the days of her giving birth were fulfilled, and there were twins in her womb.
And the firstborn came out red, all over like a hairy hide. And she gave him the name Esau.
And after this his brother came out, and his hand was grasping Esau's heel, and she called his name Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when Rebekah bore them.
These young men grew up. And Esau was a man skilled in hunting, but Jacob was a blameless man who stayed at home.
Isaac loved Esau, and his game was food for him; and Rebekah loved Jacob.
Jacob cooked a stew. Esau came from the field, exhausted.
Esau said to Jacob: "Let me taste some of that wheat stew of yours, for I am faint." For this reason his name was called Edom.
Jacob said to Esau: "Give me your birthright today."
Esau said to him: "Behold, I am about to die, and what use is this birthright to me?"
Jacob said to him: "Swear to me today." And he swore to him and gave his birthright to Jacob.
And Jacob gave Esau bread and a stew of lentils. He ate and drank, and rose and went away. And Esau despised his birthright.
There was a famine in the land, besides the famine that had been in the days of Abraham. Isaac went to Abimelech, the king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
The Lord appeared to him and said: "Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in the land that I tell you,

and live as a stranger in this land, and I will be with you and will bless you; and to you and to your descendants I will give all this, and I will confirm the oath that I swore to Abraham your father."
And I will multiply your offspring like the stars of heaven, and I will give to you and to your offspring all this land. And all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in your offspring,
because your father obeyed my voice and kept my commandments, my ordinances and my judgments.
And Isaac settled in Gerar.

The men of that land asked about Rebecca, his wife, and he said, "She is my sister." He was afraid to say, "She is my wife," in case the men of that place killed him because of Rebecca, his wife, for she was beautiful in appearance.
And he was there a long time. Abimelech, the king of the Gerarites, looked down through a window and saw Isaac sporting with Rebecca, his wife.
Abimelech called Isaac and said to him, "So Rebecca is your wife! Why did you say, 'She is my sister'?" Isaac said to him, "In case I died because of her."
Abimelech said to him, "What is this you have done to us? A little more and one of my kin would have carried her off, and you would have brought ignorance [i.e. a sin of ignorance] upon us."
Abimelech gave orders to all his people and said, "Anyone who touches this man or his wife shall be liable to death."
Isaac sowed in that land, and that year he had a hundredfold yield of barley. The Lord blessed him
and exalted the man. And he grew greater and greater, until he became very great.
And he had flocks of sheep and herds of cattle and a great deal of farmland. And the Philistines envied him.
And all the wells that his father's servants had dug, the Philistines stopped them up and filled them with earth.
Abimelech said to Isaac, "Go away from us, for you have become much stronger than we are."
And Isaac went away from there, and camped in the valley of Gerar, and settled there.

And afterwards Isaac dug again the wells of water that his father's servants had dug, which the Philistines had stopped up and filled with earth after the death of his father Abraham. And he gave them the same names that his father had given them.
And Isaac's servants dug a well in the valley of Gerar, and found there a well of living water.
And the herdsmen of the Gerarites quarrelled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying, "The water is ours." And he named that well Injury, because they had done him wrong.
He moved on from there and dug another well. They quarrelled over that one too, and he named it Enmity.
And he went on from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. And he named it Broad Space, and said, "For now the Lord has made room for us and has made us increase on the earth."
From there he went up to the Well of the Oath.

And the Lord appeared to him that night and said to him, "I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your offspring for the sake of Abraham, your father."
And he built an altar to the Lord there, and called on the name of the Lord, and pitched his tent there. Isaac's servants dug a well in the valley of Gerar.
And Abimelech came from Gerar to Isaac, with Ahuzzath, the steward of his household, and Phicol, the commander of his army.
And Isaac said to them, "Why have you come to me, since you hated me?"
They said, "We have clearly seen that the Lord is with you, and we said: Let there be an oath between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you,
that you will do us no harm, just as we did not despise you, and just as we treated you well and sent you away in peace. And now you are blessed by the Lord.
And he prepared bread for them. They ate and drank.
And they rose at dawn, and each man swore an oath to his companion. And Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in safety.
In those very days Isaac's servants came and told him about the well that they had dug, and said to him: "We have not found water."
And he called it "Oath." For this reason he named that city "Oath," and it is called so to this day.
Esau was forty years old, and he took as wives Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, daughter of Elon the Hivite.
And they were contentious toward Isaac and Rebecca.
And it came to pass, after Isaac had grown old, that his eyes grew too dim to see. And he called his elder son Esau and said to him: "My son." And he said: "Here I am."
Isaac said to him: "Behold, I have grown old, and I do not know the day of my death.
Now take your gear, your quiver and bow, and go out into the field and hunt game for me,
and make me food such as I love, and bring it to me. Let me eat, and my soul will bless you before I die."
But Rebecca was listening as Isaac spoke to his son Esau. And Esau, Jacob's brother, went out into the field to hunt game for his father.
And Rebecca said to Jacob, her younger son: "Behold, I heard your father speaking to your brother Esau, and he said:
'Hunt game for me and make me food. Let me eat, and I will bless you before the Lord before I die.'
Now, my son, listen to me and do as I command you.
Go to the flock and bring me two young, good kids, and I will make them into food for your father, such as he loves.
And take it in to your father, and he will eat, and your father will bless you before his death."
Jacob said to his mother Rebecca: "My brother Esau is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
Perhaps my father will touch me with his hand, and I will seem to him like someone mocking him, and I will bring a curse upon myself and not a blessing."
His mother said to him: "Let that curse be upon me, my son! Only listen to my voice, and go and bring them to me."
So he went and took them and brought them to his mother. And his mother made food such as his father loved.
And Rebecca took the fine clothing of her son Esau, which was kept with her in the house, and put it on Jacob, her younger son.
And she wrapped the skins of the kids around his arms and over the bare part of his neck.
And she put the food and the bread that she had made into the hands of her son Jacob.
And he brought it in to his father and said: "Father." And he said: "Here I am. Who are you, my son?"
And Jacob said to his father, "I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Get up, sit, and eat of my game, so that your soul may bless me."
And Isaac said to his son, "How is it that you found it so quickly, my son?" And he said, "Because the Lord your God brought it before me."
Isaac said to Jacob, "Come near, and let me touch you with my hand, my son, to know whether you are my son Esau or not."
And Jacob came near to Isaac his father, and he touched him with his hand. And he said, "This voice is the voice of Jacob, but these hands are the hands of Esau."
And he did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like the hands of Esau. And he blessed him.
And he said, "Are you my son Esau?" And he said, "I am."
And he said, "Bring me some of your game and let me eat, my son, so that my soul may bless you." And he brought it to him, and he ate. And he brought him wine, and he drank.
And Isaac his father said to him, "Come near to me and kiss me, my son."

And he came near and kissed him. And he smelled the fragrance of his clothing, and he blessed him and said, "Behold, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a full field which the Lord has blessed.
May the Lord give you of the dew of heaven and of the fatness of the earth, and an abundance of wheat and wine;

and may nations serve you and princes bow down to you; and be lord over your brother, and may the sons of your father bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed, and may those who bless you be blessed!"
And as soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob his son, and Jacob had gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came in from hunting.
And he prepared food for his father and said to him, "Let my father get up and eat of his son's game, so that your soul may bless me."
And Isaac his father said to him, "Who are you?" And he said to him, "I am Esau, your firstborn son."
Isaac was seized with very great astonishment and said, "Who then was it who hunted game for me and brought it to me, and I ate of it all before you came, and I blessed him? And blessed may he be!"
And when Esau heard these words of Isaac his father, he cried out with a loud and very bitter cry and said, "Bless me too, father!"
Isaac said to him, "Your brother came with deceit and took your blessing."

And Esau said, "Rightly was he named Jacob, for he has supplanted me these two times: first he took my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing." And Esau said to his father, "Have you not kept back a blessing for me, father?"
Isaac answered and said to Esau, "Since I have made him lord over you, and all his brothers servants to him, and I have sustained him with wheat and wine, what now shall I do for you, my son?"
Esau said to his father, "Do you have only one blessing, father? Bless me too." And as Isaac was distressed, Esau cried out with a loud voice and wept.
Isaac his father answered and said to him, "Behold, your dwelling shall be away from the fatness of the earth and from the dew of heaven above.
By your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother. But the time will come when you break free and throw off his yoke from your neck."

And Esau held a grudge against Jacob his brother because of the blessing his father had blessed him with. And Esau said in his mind: "Let the days of my father's death come near, and I will kill Jacob my brother."
Rebekah was told these words of her elder son. And she sent for her younger son, called him, and said to him: "Look, your brother is threatening to kill you.
Now, my child, listen to my voice: get up and flee to Laban my brother, to Haran,
and stay with him for some days,
until your brother's anger and wrath turn away from you and he forgets what you did to him. Then I will send for you and call you back from there. Why should I lose both of you in a single day?"
And Rebekah said to Isaac: "I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob also takes a wife from the daughters of this land, what is my life worth?"
Isaac called Jacob and blessed him. He commanded him and said: "Do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.
Get up and go to Mesopotamia, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father, and take a wife for yourself from there, a daughter of Laban, your mother's brother.
And may my God bless you, make you increase and multiply, and may you become an assembly of peoples;
and may he give you the blessing of Abraham my father, so that you and your descendants after you may inherit this land where you are a sojourner, which God gave to Abraham."
And Isaac sent Jacob away. And Jacob got up and went to Mesopotamia, to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.

Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and that Jacob had gone to Mesopotamia of Syria to take a wife for himself. He saw that when Isaac blessed him he had commanded him, saying: "Do not take a wife from the daughters of the Canaanites,"
and that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and gone to Mesopotamia.
And Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were displeasing in the sight of Isaac his father.
So Esau went to Ishmael, son of Abraham, and took Mahalath, daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth, as a wife in addition to the wives he already had.
And Jacob went out from the Well of the Oath and went toward Haran.
And he came to a certain place and slept there, because the sun had set. He took a stone from among the stones of that place, put it under his head as a pillow, and lay down in that place.
And he saw a vision: and behold, a ladder was set up on the earth, and its top reached to heaven, and the angels of God were going up and coming down on it.

And the Lord stood firmly above it, and said: "I am the Lord, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. Do not be afraid! The land on which you are sleeping I will give to you and to your descendants.

And your descendants will be like the sand of the sea, and they will spread out toward the sea, and to the north, and to the south, and to the east. And all the tribes of the earth will be blessed through you and through your descendants.
And behold, I am with you to protect you on all your ways, wherever you go. And I will bring you back to this same land, for I will not leave you until I have done everything I have told you."
Jacob woke up from his sleep and said: "God is in this place, and I did not know it."
And he was afraid and said, "How terrible is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and these are the gates of heaven."
And Jacob rose early in the morning and took the stone that he had put there under his head as a pillow, and he set it up as a pillar and poured oil on the top of the stone.
And he called that place House of God. And the name of that city at first was Ulamluz.
And Jacob made a vow and said, "If God will be with me and keep me on this way on which I am going, and give me bread to eat and clothing to put on,
and bring me back alive to the house of my [?] father, then the Lord shall be my God,
and this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be a house of my God; and of everything, as much as you give me, I will give a tenth to you."
And Jacob set out and went to the land of the east, to Laban the Syrian, son of Bethuel, the brother of Rebecca, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
And he looked and saw a well in the field. And there were flocks of sheep there, resting there, for from that well they watered the flock. And a great stone lay over the mouth of that well.

And all the flocks and the shepherds would gather there, and they would roll the stone away from the mouth of the well and water the sheep, and then put the stone back over the mouth of the well, in its place.
Jacob said to them, "Brothers, where are you from?" And they said to him, "We are from Haran."
Jacob said to them, "Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?" And they said to him, "We know him."
He said to them, "Is he well?" And they said to him, "He is well." And while he was saying this, behold, Rachel was coming with her father's sheep.
And Jacob said, "The day is still high, and it is not yet time for the flocks to be gathered. Water the sheep and go and pasture them."
But they said to him, "We cannot, until all the shepherds have gathered and they roll this stone away from the mouth of the well; then we will water them."
While he was still speaking with them, behold, Rachel was coming with her father's sheep, for she pastured her father's sheep.

And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of Laban, his mother's brother, Jacob went up and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered the sheep of Laban, his mother's brother.
And Jacob kissed Rachel, and Jacob cried out with a loud voice and wept.
And he told Rachel that he was Rebecca's son. And Rachel ran and told her father according to these words.

And it came to pass, when Laban heard the name of Jacob, his sister's son, he ran to meet him, and embraced him and kissed him. And he brought him into his house, and Jacob told Laban all these things.
And Laban said to him, "You are of my bones and of my flesh." And he stayed with him many days and months.
And Laban said to Jacob, "Because you are my brother, you shall not serve me for nothing. Tell me, what are your wages?"
Now Laban had two daughters. The name of the elder was Leah, and of the younger Rachel.
And Leah's eyes were weak, but Rachel was lovely to look at and beautiful of face.
Jacob loved Rachel, and he said, "I will serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter."
Laban said to him, "It is better for me to give her to you than to give her to another man. Stay with me."
And Jacob served seven years for Rachel. And they seemed to him like a few days because of his love for her.
Jacob said to Laban: “Give me my wife, for my days of service are completed, so that I may go in to her.”
Laban gathered all the men of that place and made a wedding feast.
And it was evening. And Laban took Leah his daughter and brought her in to Jacob. And Jacob went in to her.
And he gave Leah his daughter Zilpah, his maidservant, as a maidservant for her.
And it was morning, and behold, it was Leah! Jacob said to Laban: “Why have you done this? Did I not serve you for Rachel? And why have you treated me with contempt?”
And Laban said: “It is not so in our place, to give the younger before the elder.
Complete another seven years for this one, and I will give you this one too, for the work that you will do for me, yet another seven years.”
And Jacob did so and completed the other seven years. And Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
And he gave Rachel his daughter Bilhah, his maidservant, as a maidservant for her.
And he went in to Rachel, and he loved Rachel more than Leah, and he served him yet another seven years.
And the Lord saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.
Leah conceived and bore Jacob a son. And she called his name Reuben and said: “For the Lord has seen my humiliation and has given me a child. Now my husband will love me.”
And again she conceived and bore a second son and said: “The Lord has heard that I am hated, and he has given me this one too.” And she called his name Simeon.
And again she conceived and bore a son and said: “From now on my husband will be joined to me, for I have borne him three sons.” Therefore she called his name Levi.
And again she conceived and bore a son and said: “Now once more I will praise the Lord.” Therefore she called his name Judah. And she stopped bearing.
When Rachel saw that she had not borne Jacob a son, Rachel envied her sister and said to Jacob: “Give me a child; if not, I shall die.”
Jacob became angry with Rachel and said to her: “Am I God, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?”
Rachel said to him: “Here is Bilhah, my maidservant. Go in to her, and let her bear upon my knees, and I too will have children through her.”
And she gave him Bilhah, her maidservant, as a wife, and Jacob went in to her.
And Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, conceived and bore Jacob a son.
And Rachel said: “The Lord has judged in my favour and has heard my voice and has given me a son.” Therefore she called his name Dan.
And Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.
And Rachel said: “God has helped me, and I have become equal to my sister and have prevailed.” And she called his name Naphtali.
And when Leah saw that she had stopped bearing, she took Zilpah, her maidservant, and gave her to Jacob as a wife.
Zilpah, Leah's maidservant, conceived. And she bore Jacob a son.
And she named him Gad.
And afterwards Zilpah the maidservant conceived and bore Jacob a second son.
And Leah said: "Blessed am I, for the women will call me blessed." And she named him Asher.
In the days of the wheat harvest Reuben went out and found mandrakes in the field, and he brought them to Leah his mother. And Rachel said to Leah her sister: "Give me your son's mandrakes."

Leah said to her: "Is it not enough for you that you have taken my husband from me? Will you now take my son's mandrakes too?" Rachel said to her: "Very well, then, let him go in to you this night in exchange for your son's mandrakes."

Jacob came in from the field in the evening. And Leah went out to meet him and said: "You shall come in to me today, for I have bought you in exchange for my son's mandrakes." And he went in to her that night.
And God heard Leah. And she conceived and bore Jacob a fifth son.
And Leah said: "The Lord has given me my wage, because I gave my maidservant to my husband." And she named him Issachar, which means "wage."
And Leah conceived and bore Jacob a sixth son.
And Leah said: "God has given me a good gift. From this time on my husband will look on me with favour, for I have borne him six sons." And she named him Zebulun.
And after this she bore a daughter and named her Dinah.
And God remembered Rachel, and he heard her and opened her womb.
And she conceived and bore Jacob a son, and Rachel said: "God has taken away my reproach."
And she named him Joseph and said: "May God add another child to me."
And when Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban: "Send me away, so that I may go to my own land.
Give me my wives, for whom I have served you, so that I may go, for you know the service I have given you."
Laban said to him: "If I have found favour in your sight, for the Lord has blessed me since you came,
name your wage to me and I will give it to you."
Jacob said to him: "You know how I have served you, and how great your flock became with me.
For what you had before I came was little, and it has grown into a multitude, and the Lord has blessed you wherever I set my foot. Now, then, let me build a house for myself too."
Laban said to him: "What shall I give you?" Jacob said to him: "Do not give me anything. If you will do what I say, I will go on tending your flocks and keeping them.
Bring out all your flock today, and from it separate every white sheep among the lambs, and every bright and white one among the goats. Let this be my wage.
My righteousness will answer for me on this day, tomorrow, for this is my wage before you: everything that is white among the lambs, and bright and speckled among the goats [?]"
Laban said to him: "Let it be as you say!"

And on that day he separated out the speckled and white he-goats, and every speckled and white she-goat, and everything white that was among them, and every white one among the lambs. And he gave them into the hands of his sons, each flock by itself.
And he put a distance of three days' journey between them and Jacob. And Jacob tended the rest of Laban's sheep.
But Jacob took fresh rods of [?] and of walnut and of zelkova, and Jacob peeled them, stripping off their fresh bark. And the white where he had peeled them showed on the rods, speckled.
And he set the rods in the troughs at the watering places, so that when the sheep came to drink in front of the rods, they would come to drink and the sheep would look at the rods.
And the sheep bore white and speckled young, and young spotted with ash colour.
And Jacob separated the lambs, and in front of the sheep he set a whitish ram and every speckled one among the lambs. And he kept his own flock apart by itself and did not mix it with Laban's sheep.
And at the time when the sheep came into heat and conceived, Jacob would put the rods in front of the sheep at the watering place, so that they would conceive after the likeness of the rods.
And when they were giving birth, he did not put them there. So the unmarked ones were Laban's, and the marked ones were Jacob's.
And the man grew very greatly rich, and he had very many flocks, and cattle, and male and female servants, camels and donkeys.
And Jacob heard the words of Laban's sons, who were saying: "Jacob has taken from us everything that was our father's, and from what was our father's he has gained all this wealth."

And Jacob saw Laban's face, and it was not toward him as it had been yesterday and the day before. The Lord said to Jacob: "Return to the land of your father and of your kindred, and I will be with you."
And Jacob sent and called Leah and Rachel to the field where the flock was.
And he said to them: "I see your father's face, that it is not toward me as it was yesterday and the day before. But the God of my father has been with me.
And you yourselves know that I have served your father with all my strength.
But your father cheated me and changed my wages of ten lambs, and God did not allow him to do me harm.
If he said, 'The speckled shall be your wages,' all the sheep would bear speckled young. If he said, 'The white shall be your wages,' all the sheep would bear white young.
And God has taken away all your father's sheep and given them to me.

And at the time when the sheep were in heat and conceiving, I saw with my own eyes in a dream: and behold, the he-goats and rams that were mounting the sheep and goats were white and speckled and spotted with ash colour.
And the angel of the Lord said to me in the dream: 'Jacob, Jacob.' And I said: 'What is it?'
And he said: 'Lift up your eyes and see the he-goats and rams mounting the sheep and goats, speckled and spotted with ash colour, for I have seen what Laban is doing to you.

I am your God, who appeared to you in the place of God, where you anointed my pillar and made a vow to me. Now arise, go out from this land, and go to the land of your birth, and I will be with you.'"
Leah and Rachel answered and said to him: "Is there still any portion or inheritance for us in our father's house?
Are we not counted by him as strangers? For he sold us, and he has completely used up our money.
All the wealth and glory that God has taken from our father is ours and our children's. Now, whatever your Lord has told you, do it."
Jacob rose, took his wives and children, and set them on camels.
He took all his property and all his goods [?] that he had acquired in Mesopotamia, and everything that was his, and set out to go to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan.
Now Laban had gone to [?shear] his sheep. Rachel stole her father's idols.
Jacob hid from Laban the Aramean and did not tell him that he was fleeing.
He fled with everything he had. He crossed the river and headed for the mountain of Gilead.
On the third day Laban the Aramean was told that Jacob had fled.
He took all his kinsmen with him and pursued Jacob for seven days' journey, and overtook him at the mountain of Gilead.
God came to Laban at night in a vision and said to him: "Be careful not to speak harshly to Jacob."
Laban overtook Jacob. Jacob had pitched his tent on the mountain, and Laban stationed his kinsmen on the mountain of Gilead.
Laban said to Jacob: "What have you done? Why did you flee in secret? You stole from me and carried off my daughters like captives taken by the sword.
If you had told me, I would have sent you off with joy and music, with drums and lyre.
Was I not worthy to kiss my children and my daughters? Now you have acted foolishly.
Now it is in my power to do you harm. But the God of your father said to me yesterday: 'Be careful not to say anything evil to Jacob.'
Now, if you have left because your heart longed to go to your father's house, why did you steal my gods?"

Jacob answered and said to Laban: "Because I was afraid, and I said, 'He might take his daughters away from me, and everything I have.' Find whatever of yours is with me and take it." And he found nothing of his with him, not one thing.
Jacob answered and said: "Whoever you find your gods with, let him not live, in front of our kinsmen." Jacob did not know that Rachel his wife had stolen them.

Laban went in and searched all of Leah's things and found nothing. He came out of Leah's tent and searched Jacob's tent and found nothing, and the tents of both maidservants, and found nothing. Then he went into Rachel's tent.
Rachel had taken the idols, put them under the camels' saddles, and sat on them.
She said to her father: "Do not be offended, my lord, that I cannot get up, for the way of women is upon me." Laban searched all the tents and did not find the idols.
Jacob became angry and quarrelled with Laban. Jacob answered and said to Laban: "What is my wrong, and what is my sin, that you pursue me
and have searched all the goods of my house? What have you found of all the goods of your house? Set it here in front of all your kinsmen and my kinsmen, and let them judge between the two of us.
I have been with you these twenty years. Your ewes and your she-goats did not miscarry, and I did not eat the rams of your flock.
I never brought you anything torn by wild beasts. I myself made good whatever was stolen by day or by night.
I was worn down by the heat of the day and the frost of the night, and sleep was taken away from my eyes.
These twenty years I have been in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks, and I made light of all my wages on account of those ten lambs.
If the God of my father Abraham and the Fear of Isaac had not been with me, you would now have sent me away empty-handed. God saw my humiliation and my toil, and he rebuked you yesterday.

Laban answered Jacob and said to him: "These daughters are my daughters, these sons are my sons, and these flocks are my flocks. All that you see is mine. And what am I to do today about my daughters?
Now come, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it be a witness between you and me." And he said: "See, there is no one with me; see, the Lord is witness between me and you."
Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.

And Jacob said to his kinsmen: "Gather stones." They gathered stones and raised a mound, and they ate and drank there beside the mound. And Laban said: "This mound is a witness between me and you today."
Laban called it the Mound of Witness, and Jacob called it the Mound-Witness.

And Laban said to Jacob: "Here is this mound and the pillar that you have set up between you and me. This mound bears witness, and this pillar bears witness too." For this reason it was named the Mound of Witness.
"And the vision that he saw: may God watch between me and you, for we are about to part from each other.
If you mistreat my daughters, or if you take other wives besides my daughters, take note: there is no one here with us.
If I do not cross over to you, then you are not to cross over to me past this mound of mine and this pillar with evil intent.
May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor judge between us."
And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac. Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and called all his kinsmen, and they ate, drank and went to sleep.
Laban rose early in the morning, kissed his sons and blessed them, then turned back and went to his own place.
And Jacob went on his way in peace. Jacob raised his eyes and saw the camp of God encamped, and the angels of God, encamped, met him.
When Jacob saw them he said: "This is the camp of God." And he named that place Camps.
Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau,
and he instructed them, saying: "Say this to my lord Esau: 'Your servant Jacob says this: I have been living as a sojourner with Laban and have stayed until now,
and I have acquired cattle and donkeys, flocks, menservants and maidservants. I have sent to tell my lord Esau, so that your servant may find favour in your sight.'"
Jacob's messengers came back and said to him: "We went to your brother Esau, and he too is coming to meet you, with four hundred men."
Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed. He divided the people who were with him, and the flocks and the cattle, into two camps.
And Jacob said: "If Esau comes to one camp and destroys it, the other will escape."
And Jacob said: O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, O Lord, who said to me, "Go to the land of your birth, and it will go well with you."
I am more than repaid by all the righteousness and all the truth that you have shown your servant, for I crossed this Jordan with only this staff, and now, behold, I have become two camps.
Deliver me, O Lord, from the hands of my brother Esau, for I am afraid of him, that he may come and kill me, and the mothers with the children.
And you said, "I will surely do you good, and I will make your offspring like the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted because there is so much of it."
And he slept there that night. And he took what he had brought as a gift and sent it to his brother Esau:
two hundred she-goats, twenty he-goats,
thirty milch camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls.
And he put each flock separately into the hands of his servants and said to them: Go on ahead of me, and keep a space between one flock and the next.
And he commanded the first one, saying: If my brother Esau meets you and questions you, saying, "Whose are you, and where are you going, and whose are these that are going ahead of you?"
tell him: "They belong to your servant Jacob. He has sent them as a gift to his lord Esau, and look, he himself is coming behind us."
And he gave the same command to the first, the second and the third, and to all who went ahead of him, saying: Speak to Esau in these words when he finds you,

and say, "Look, your servant Jacob is coming behind us." For he said: I will appease him with this gift that I have sent ahead of me, and after that I will see his face. Who knows, perhaps he will receive me kindly.
And the gift went on ahead of him, but he slept that night in the camp.
And he got up in the night and took his two wives, his two maidservants and his eleven children, and crossed the ravine,
and he brought across everything that he had.
And he stayed there alone. And a man wrestled with him until dawn.
When the man saw that he could not overpower him, he touched the broad part of his thigh, and the broad part of Jacob's thigh went numb as he wrestled with him.
