And he said: Let me go, for dawn has broken. But Jacob said: I will not let you go until you bless me.
And he said to him: What is your name? And he said: Jacob.
He said to him: From now on your name will no longer be Jacob, but your name will be Israel, for you have struggled with God and prevailed, and you are strong with men as well.
Jacob asked him, saying: Tell me, what is your name? And he said: Why do you ask my name? It is wonderful. And he blessed him there.
And he named that place "Vision of God," for he said, "I have seen God face to face, and my life was spared."
And the sun rose upon him. As that Vision of God passed, he was limping because of his thigh.

For this reason the children of Israel do not eat the sinew that went numb, which is on the broad part of the thigh, to this very day, because he touched the broad part of Jacob's thigh, which went numb.
Jacob looked up and saw his brother Esau coming, with four hundred men. And Jacob divided the children among Leah, Rachel and the two maidservants.
And he placed the two maidservants and their sons first, Leah and her children after them, and Rachel and Joseph last.
And Jacob went on ahead of them and bowed down to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.
And Esau ran to meet him, embraced him and kissed him, and laid his face on Jacob's neck; and the two of them wept.
And he looked up and saw his two wives and the children, and said: "Who are these to you?" And he said: "These are the children with whom God has shown mercy to your servant."
And the maidservants and their children came near and bowed down.
And Leah and her children came near and bowed down. And after this Rachel and Joseph came and bowed down.
And Esau said: "Are all these camps that I met yours?" And Jacob said to him: "They are so that your servant might find favour before you, my lord."
Esau said to him: "I have a great deal. Keep what is yours for yourself!"
Jacob said to him: "If I have found favour before you, accept this gift from my hands. For I have seen your face as one sees the face of God; be well-disposed toward me,
and accept this blessing which I have brought you, for God has shown me mercy and I have a great deal." And he urged him, and he accepted it.
Esau: "Let us get up and go straight on."
Jacob said to him: "My lord knows that my children are tender, and the cattle and sheep are just giving birth. If I drive them hard for one day, or even two days, the whole flock will die.
Let my lord go on ahead of his servant, and I will manage to travel at leisure on the road, at the pace of what is before me and behind the children, until I come to my lord at Seir."
Esau said to him: "I will leave with you some of the people who are with me." But Jacob said: "Why this? It is enough that I have found favour before you, my lord."
And Esau returned that same day to Seir.
And Jacob went on to Tents (Succoth), and built himself a house there and made shelters for his flock. For this reason he named that place Tents.
And Jacob came to Salem, a city of the Shechemites, which is in the land of Canaan, when he was coming from Mesopotamia of Syria, and he encamped facing that city.
And there he bought the portion of the field where he had pitched his tent from Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred lambs.
And he set up an altar there and called on the name of the God of Israel.
Dinah, the daughter of Leah whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of that country.
And Shechem, the son of Hamor the Horite, the ruler of that land, saw her; he took her and lay with her and humbled her.
And his soul clung to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the maiden and spoke to her according to the maiden's mind.
Shechem spoke to Hamor his father and said: "Get me this girl as a wife."
Jacob heard that Shechem the son of Hamor had defiled his daughter Dinah. But Jacob's sons were with his flock out in the field, and Jacob kept silent until they came.
Hamor, the father of Shechem, went out to Jacob to speak with him.

Then the sons of Jacob came in from the field. When they heard this, the men were deeply grieved, because a shameful thing had been done in Israel: he had lain with Jacob's daughter, and that was not fitting.
Hamor spoke to them and said: "My son Shechem has chosen your daughter with all his soul. Give her to him as his wife.
Intermarry with us: give us your daughters, and give our daughters in marriage to your sons.
Settle among us, and see, the land is wide before you. Live in it, trade in it, and acquire property in it."
Shechem said to her father and to her brothers: "Let me find favour in your sight, and whatever you say, I will give you.
Make the price in property very great, and I will give whatever you tell me; only give me this girl as my wife."
The sons of Jacob answered Shechem and his father Hamor, and they spoke with deceit, because he had defiled their sister.
Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, said to them: "We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to an uncircumcised man, for that would be a disgrace to us.
Only on this condition will we agree with you and settle among you: if you become as we are, so that every male among you is circumcised.
Then we will give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters for ourselves. We will settle among you and become one people.
But if you do not listen to us and be circumcised, we will take our daughters and go away."
These words pleased Hamor and Shechem, Hamor's son.
The young man did not delay to do this, because he desired Jacob's daughter. He was the most honoured man in his father's house.
Hamor and Shechem came to the gate of their city, and they spoke to the men of their city, saying:
"These men are at peace with us. Let them settle in the land and trade in it, for see, the land is wide before them. Let us take their daughters as our wives, and let us give them ours.
But only on this condition will these men agree to live with us and become one people with us: that we are circumcised, just as they are circumcised.
Will not their livestock, their possessions and all their four-footed animals be ours? Only let us agree with them on this, and they will settle among us."
All who went out through the gate of their city listened to Hamor and his son Shechem, and every male was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
On the third day, while they were still in pain, two of Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, each took his sword. They entered the city and killed every male.
They killed Hamor and Shechem with the edge of the sword, took their sister Dinah out of Shechem's house, and left.
Then the sons of Jacob came upon the slain and plundered the whole city, because their sister Dinah had been defiled.
They carried off their sheep, their cattle and their donkeys, everything that was in the city and everything that was in the field.
They took captive all their women and children and their wives, and carried off all their goods. They plundered everything that was in the city and everything that was in the houses.

Jacob said to Simeon and Levi: "You have made me hateful, so that I am regarded as evil by all who live in this city, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. I am few in number. They will gather against me and destroy me, and I and my house will be wiped out."
But they said: "Should our sister then have been treated like a harlot?"
God said to Jacob: "Arise and go up to Bethel and live there. Build an altar there to God, who appeared to you when you were fleeing from your brother Esau."
Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him: "Put away the idols of the foreigners that are among you. Purify yourselves and change your clothing."
"Arise, and let us go up to Bethel and make an altar there to God, who heard me in all my distress, who was with me and delivered me on the road I travelled."

And they gave Jacob the foreigners' idols that were in their hands, and the earrings that were in their ears. Jacob hid them under the terebinth that was at Shechem, and destroyed them to this present day.
And Jacob set out from Shechem. The fear of God was on their city and the area around it, and they did not pursue the sons of Israel.
Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, that is, Bethel, he and all the people who were with him.
He built an altar there and named it Bethel, for God had appeared to him there when he was fleeing from his brother.
Deborah, Rebecca's nurse, died and was buried under the oak. He named that oak the Oak of Mourning.
God appeared to Jacob again at Luz, when he was coming from Mesopotamia of Syria. God blessed him
and said to him: "Your name shall no longer be Jacob; Israel shall be your name."
God said to him: "I am your God. Increase and multiply. Nations and assemblies of peoples shall come from you, and kings shall come forth from your loins."
"And the land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you. It shall be yours and your descendants' after you."
And God went up from the place where he had been speaking with him.
Jacob set up a pillar in the place where God had spoken with him, a pillar of stone. He offered an offering on it and poured oil on it.
And Jacob named the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.
His tent was moved from there to beyond the tower of Gader. When he drew near to Chabratha, on the way to the land of Ephrath, Rachel gave birth, and her labour was hard.
While she was in hard labour, the midwife said to her: "Do not be afraid, for this one too is a son for you."
As her soul was departing, for she was dying, she named him "Son of my Pain." But his father called him Benjamin.
Rachel died and was buried on the road to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem.
Jacob set up a pillar on Rachel's grave. This is the pillar of Rachel's grave to this present day.
While Israel was living in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine. Israel heard of it, and it seemed evil to him.
Jacob had twelve sons.
The sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun.
The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
The sons of Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant: Dan and Naphtali. The sons of Zilpah, Leah's maidservant: Gad and Asher.
These are the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Mesopotamia of Syria.
Jacob came to Isaac his father, to Mamre, a city of the plain, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan, where Abraham and Isaac had dwelt.
The days of Isaac, as long as he lived, were a hundred and eighty years.
And Isaac grew weak and died and was gathered to his fathers, old and full of days. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
These are the generations of Esau, that is, Edom.
And he took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah the Hivite,
and Basemath, the daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebaioth.
Adah bore him Eliphaz, and Basemath bore him Reuel,
and Oholibamah bore him Jeush and Jalam and Korah. These are the sons of Esau who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

Esau took his wives and his sons and his daughters and every person of his household, all his possessions, all his livestock, everything he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and everything he had gained. And he went away from the land of Canaan, away from the presence of Jacob his brother.
For their possessions were very great, and the land in which they sojourned could not support them because of the abundance of their possessions.
And Esau settled on Mount Seir; that is, Edom.
These are the generations of Esau, the father of Edom, on Mount Seir.
And these are the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphaz, the son of Adah, Esau's wife, and Reuel, the son of Basemath, Esau's wife.
The sons of Eliphaz were: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
And Timna, the concubine of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, bore Amalek to Eliphaz. These are the sons of Adah, Esau's wife.
These are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the sons of Basemath, Esau's wife.
These were the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the son of Zibeon, Esau's wife. She bore to Esau Jeush and Jalam and Korah.
These were the chiefs who were sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn. The sons of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn: chief Gatam, chief Kenaz,
chief Amalek. These are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Idumea. These are the sons of Adah.

And these are the sons of Reuel, the son of Esau: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom. These are the sons of Basemath, Esau's wife.
And these are the sons of Oholibamah, Esau's wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah. These are the chiefs of Oholibamah.
And these are the sons of Esau, and these are their chiefs. These are of Edom.
These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who had settled in that land of Lotan: Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
Dishon, Ezer and Dishan. These are the chiefs of Seir the Horite in the land of Edom.
The sons of Lotan were Hori and Heman, and Lotan's sister was Timna.
These are the sons of Shobal: Gozom, Manahath, Gebel, Shepho and Onam.
These are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is the Anah who found the Iamin in the wilderness while he was pasturing the yoked beasts of his father Zibeon.
These are the children of Anah: Dishon, and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.
These are the sons of Dishon: Amada, Abama, Ithran and Cheran.
These are the sons of Ezer: Balaam, Lukam, Iovikam and Usam.
These are the sons of Rusan: Uz and Aran.
These are the chiefs of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
chief Ezer, chief Dishon, chief Dishan. These are the chiefs of the Horites according to their chiefdoms in the land of Edom.
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over Israel:
Bela son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
Bela died, and Jobab son of Zerah, of Bozrah, reigned in his place.
Jobab died, and Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
Husham died, and Hadad son of Barad reigned in his place; he struck down Midian in the plain of Moab, and the name of his city was Getem.
Hadad died, and Samlah, who was from Masrekah, reigned in his place.
Samlah died, and Saul, who was from Rehoboth, which is on the river, reigned in his place.
Saul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.
Baal-hanan died, and Hadad son of Arad reigned in his place; the name of his city was Phogor. His wife's name was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, son of Mezahab.
These are the names of the chiefs of Esau and of their tribes, according to their places, their lands and their kindred: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, chief Zephaim. These are the chiefs of Edom in their settlements.
Jacob settled in the land where his father had dwelt, in the land of Canaan.

And these are the generations of Jacob. Joseph was seventeen years old, and he was shepherding the flocks with his brothers. He was still a boy, with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father's concubines. And they laid an evil charge against Joseph before Israel, his father.
But Jacob loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was the son of his old age. And he made him a multicoloured garment of many colours.
When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, his brothers hated him and could not speak a word of peace to him at all.
Joseph had a dream and told it to his brothers,
and said: "Listen to this dream that I have had:
I thought that you were binding sheaves in the middle of the field, and my sheaf rose and stood upright. And your sheaves turned and bowed down to my sheaves."
His brothers said to him: "Will you really reign as king over us, or will you really rule as lord over us?" And they hated him even more because of those dreams of his.
Then he had another dream, and he told it to his father and his brothers, and said: "Look, I have had another dream: the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me."
His father grew angry with him and said to him: "What is this dream that you have had? Shall I and your mother and your brothers really come to bow down to you on the ground?"
And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept this saying in mind.
And his brothers went to pasture their father's flocks at Shechem.
Israel said to Joseph: "Are not your brothers pasturing the flocks at Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them." And he said to him: "Here I am."
Israel said: "Go and ask after your brothers, whether they are well, and after the flocks, and bring me word." And he sent him from the valleys of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
And a man found him wandering in the field. The man asked him: "Whom are you looking for?"
And he said to him: "I am looking for my brothers. Tell me, where are they pasturing their flocks?"
The man said to him: "They have gone from here, for I heard them saying, 'Let us go to Dothan.'" And Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.
They saw him coming from far off, and before he came near to them they plotted evil against him, to kill him.
They said to one another: "Look, here comes that dreamer."
"Now come, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits, and we will say that a wild beast devoured him. And we shall see what becomes of his dreams."
But Reuben heard this and rescued him from the hands of his brothers, and said to them: "Let us not kill him."
And he said to them: "Do not shed blood. Throw him into this pit in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him." He said this so that he might rescue him and give him back to his father.
And when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of the multicoloured garment that he was wearing,
and they took him and threw him into the pit. The pit was empty; there was no water in it.

And they sat down to eat bread, and they looked up and saw a band of Ishmaelite merchants travelling from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with incense, resin and myrrh gum, and they were going down to Egypt.
Judah said to his brothers: "What profit is there if we kill our brother and hide his blood?"
Come, let us sell him to these Ishmaelites, but let our hands not be laid on him, for he is our brother." His brothers listened to him.
And the men, the Midianite merchants, passed by, and they brought Joseph up out of the pit and sold Joseph to those Ishmaelites for twenty drachmas, and they took him down to Egypt.
Reuben came back and did not find Joseph in the pit, and he tore his clothes
and went back to his brothers and said: "The boy is not here, and I, where am I to go?"
But they took Joseph's garment and slaughtered a young goat from the flock, and they stained the garment with the blood
and they sent the many-coloured garment and brought it to his father and said: "We found this. See whether it is your son's garment or not."
And he recognized it and said: "This is my son's garment. An evil beast has devoured him; an evil beast has snatched Joseph from me."
And Jacob tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his loins, and he mourned for his son for many days.
All his sons and his daughters gathered and came to comfort him. But he did not want comfort, and he said: "I will go down to my son in Hades, mourning." And he wept for him bitterly.
But those Ishmaelite merchants sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, the eunuch, [?] (the word "matakaran-" is unclear).
And at that time Judah went away from his brothers, and he went to a certain Adullamite man whose name was Hirah.
And there Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite man, whose name was Shua. He took her and married her.
And she conceived and bore a son, and he named him Er.
And she conceived again and bore a son, and he named him Onan.
And she bore yet another son, and he named him Shelah. She was at Chezib when she bore them.
And Judah brought a wife for Er, his firstborn son, and her name was Tamar.
And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked before the Lord, and the Lord killed him.
Judah said to Onan: "Go in to your brother's wife and do a brother-in-law's duty to her, and raise up offspring for your brother."
Onan understood that the offspring would not be his. And whenever he went in to his brother's wife, he spilled his seed on the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother.
This deed was evil in the sight of God, because he did this, and the Lord put him to death as well.

Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law: "Remain a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah grows up," for he said: "Otherwise he too may die like his brothers." So Tamar went and stayed in her father's house.
The days passed, and Shua, Judah's wife, died. Judah was comforted after his mourning, and he went up to the shearers of his sheep at Timnah, he and Hirah, his Adullamite shepherd.
And they told Tamar, his daughter-in-law: "Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep."

And she took off her widow's clothes, put on other clothes, adorned herself, and sat at the gate of Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah. For she saw that Shelah, his son, had grown up, and he had not given her to him as a wife.
And Judah saw her and thought she was a prostitute, for she had covered her face, and he did not recognize her.
And he turned aside from his way and said to her, "Let me come in to you." For he did not recognize that she was his son's wife. And she said to him, "What will you give me if you come in to me?"
And Judah said to her, "I will send you a young goat from the flock." And she said to him, "Give me a pledge until you send it to me."

And Judah said to her, "What pledge shall I give you?" And she said, "Your ring and your necklace, and that staff you have in your hand." And he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
And she rose and took off her garment and put on the garment of her widowhood.
And Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his shepherd to get the pledge back from the woman. But he did not find her.
He asked the men of that place, "Where is the harlot who was at Enan by the road?" And they said, "There is no harlot here."
And the shepherd returned to Judah and said, "I did not find her. And the men of that place said, 'There is no harlot here.'"
Judah said, "Let her keep them! But we must not be made a laughingstock. I sent the young goat, and you did not find her."
And after three months Judah was told, "Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the harlot, and she is with child by harlotry." Judah said, "Bring her out and burn her with fire."
And as she was being led out, she sent to her father-in-law and said, "I am with child by the man to whom this pledge belongs. Recognize this ring and necklace and staff."
And Judah recognized them and said, "Tamar is more righteous than I, for I did not give her to Shelah my son." And he did not know her again.
And when she was giving birth, there were twins in her womb.
One of them put out a hand. The midwife took it and tied a scarlet thread on his hand, and said, "This one came out first."
And as he drew his hand back in, his brother came out at once, and the midwife said, "Why has a breach been opened for you?" And the one who came out first, she called his name Perez.
And after him, Zerah.
Now Joseph was brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, Pharaoh's eunuch, the chief cook, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hands of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a successful man, and he was in the house of that Egyptian man, before [him].
And his master knew that the Lord was with him, and that whatever he did, the Lord made it prosper for him.
And Joseph found favor before him, and he pleased him. And he set him over his house and gave everything he had into Joseph's hands.

And after he had set him over his house and over everything he had, the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake, and the blessing of the Lord was on all his possessions, in the house and in the field.
And he gave everything he had into Joseph's hands, and he knew nothing of what Joseph was doing except the bread that he ate. And Joseph was handsome in form and very fair of face.
After these things, the wife of his Egyptian master cast her eyes on Joseph and said to him, "Lie with me."
But he refused and said to his master's wife, "If my master knows nothing of what concerns me in his house, and has given everything there is into my hands

And no one in this house is greater than I in anything, neither inside nor outside; whatever there is, is in my hand, except only you. For you are his wife. So how can I do this evil thing and sin before my God?!
And when she spoke to him day after day, and Joseph would not agree to lie with her or to be with her,
there came such a day when Joseph went into the house to do his work, and no one was in the house.
And she grabbed Joseph's garment and said to him, "Lie with me." But Joseph left his garment in her hands and fled and went outside.
And when she saw that he had left his garment in her hands and fled. He went outside
and she called those who were in the house, and spoke to them and said: "See now, he has brought a Hebrew servant in to me to mock me. He came in to me to lie with me. I cried out with a loud voice.
And when he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garment with me, fled and went outside."
And she kept his garment with her until his master came to his house.
And she told him the same story and said: "This Hebrew servant, whom you brought in to mock me, came in to me and said to me, 'Let me lie with you.'
And when I heard this, I raised my voice and cried out. He left his garment with me and fled and went outside."
And when his master heard these words that his wife told him, saying, "This is what my servant did to me?", he was enraged with anger.
And Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison, in the place where the king's prisoners were held in the prison.
And the Lord was with Joseph and showed him mercy, and he found favour with the chief jailer.
And the chief jailer put the prison into Joseph's hands, and all the prisoners, as many as were in the prison.
The chief of the prison himself knew nothing, not even one thing, because everything was in Joseph's hands, since the Lord was with him. And whatever he did, the Lord made it prosper in his hands.
And after these things the chief cupbearer and the chief baker sinned against the king of the Egyptians.
And King Pharaoh was angry with both of his eunuchs, the cupbearer and the chief baker,
and he put them in the prison of the chief of the cooks, in the place where Joseph was imprisoned.
And the chief jailer entrusted them to Joseph, and he attended them, and they were in that prison for many days.
And both of them saw a dream, each of them, on one night, each with his own dream to be seen. The cupbearer and the chief baker of King Pharaoh saw them in that prison.
Joseph came in to them in the morning and saw them, and they were troubled.
He questioned Pharaoh's eunuchs who were in the prison of his master and said, "Why are your faces troubled today?"
And they said to him, "We have seen a dream, and there is no one to interpret it." Joseph said to them, "Does not the interpretation of dreams come from God? Tell it to me."
And the cupbearer told his dream to Joseph and said, "In my sleep I saw, and there was a vine before me,
And on the vine there were three roots. And it sprouted, the shoot grew up, and its clusters of grapes were ripe.
And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand. I took the grapes in my hand and squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup.
Joseph said to him: "This is its interpretation: the three roots are three days.

Three more days will pass, and Pharaoh will remember your office and will restore you to your post as wine-steward. You will put the cup into Pharaoh's hand as you did in your former office, when you were his cupbearer [?].
But remember me yourself when things go well for you. Do me a kindness and mention me before Pharaoh, so that he will bring me out of this prison.
For I was stolen away from the land of the Hebrews, and here too I have done nothing wrong, yet they have thrown me into this dungeon."
When the chief baker saw that he had interpreted correctly, he said to Joseph: "I too saw a dream. I thought that I had three baskets of fine flour on my head.
And in the uppermost basket there was every kind of food that King Pharaoh eats, made by the chief baker, and the birds of the sky were eating it out of the basket that was on my head."
Joseph answered and said: "This is its interpretation: these three baskets are three days.
Three more days will pass, and Pharaoh will cut off your head and hang you on a tree, and the birds of the sky will eat your flesh."
And on the third day it was Pharaoh's birthday, and he held a great feast for all his servants. And among his servants he remembered the office of the wine-steward and the office of the chief baker.
He restored the wine-steward to his own office, and he put the cup into Pharaoh's hand.
But he hanged the chief baker on a tree, just as Joseph had interpreted to him.
But the wine-steward did not remember Joseph. Instead he forgot him.
And after two years from those days, Pharaoh saw a dream. He thought that he was standing by the river.
And behold, it seemed that seven cows were coming up out of the river, beautiful in appearance and fat in flesh, and they were grazing on the bank of the river.
And seven other cows came up after them out of the same river, ugly to look at and lean in flesh, and they grazed beside the other cows on the riverbank.
And the seven cows that were ugly to look at and lean in flesh ate up the seven cows that were good to look at and choice in flesh. Pharaoh woke up.
And he saw a second dream: and behold, seven ears of grain came up on a single stalk, choice and good.
And behold, after them seven more ears sprang up, thin and blighted.
And the seven thin and blighted ears ate up the seven choice ears, full and good. Pharaoh woke up, and behold, it had been a dream.

And when morning came, his spirit was troubled within him. He sent and summoned all the interpreters of Egypt and all its wise men, and Pharaoh told them the dream. But none of them could tell Pharaoh what the dream meant.
Then the wine-steward spoke to Pharaoh and said: "Today I call my sin to mind."
Pharaoh was angry with his servants and put us in prison, in the house of the chief cook: me and the chief baker.
And we saw a dream in one night, I and he; each of us saw a dream of his own.
And there was a young Hebrew there with us, a servant of the chief cook. We told him the dream, and he interpreted it for us.
And as he interpreted it for us, so it happened to us: I was restored to this office of mine, and he was hanged on a tree and died.
Pharaoh sent and summoned Joseph and brought him out of the prison. They cut his hair and changed his clothes, and he came before Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Joseph: "I have had a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. But I have heard of you that when a dream is told to you, you interpret it."
Joseph answered Pharaoh: "Without God no answer will be given for the well-being of Pharaoh."
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph and said: "In my sleep it seemed to me that I was standing on the bank of the river,
and seven cows, choice in flesh and fine to look at, came up out of the river and were grazing on the bank.
Then seven other cows came up after them out of the same river, wretched, loathsome to look at and lean in flesh. I have never seen such loathsome ones in all of Egypt.
And the seven lean, loathsome cows ate up the seven good, choice cows.
They went into their bellies, but nothing showed that they had gone into their bellies, and they looked just as loathsome as before. I woke up and fell asleep again.
Then I saw another dream: seven ears of grain, full and good, came up in one place.
Then seven more ears, thin and blighted, sprang up beside them.
And the seven thin, blighted ears swallowed up the seven full, good ears. I told this to these interpreters, and there is no one who could explain it to me."
Joseph said to Pharaoh: "Pharaoh's dream is one. God has shown Pharaoh all that he is about to do.
The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven ears of grain are seven years. Both of Pharaoh's dreams are one.
And the seven lean cows that came up after them are seven years, and the seven thin, blighted ears of grain mean that there will be seven years of famine.
This is what I told Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh all that he is about to do.
Look, seven years of great plenty are coming in all the land of Egypt.
After them will come seven years of famine. The famine will make the plenty and abundance in the land of Egypt forgotten, and it will destroy the land.
The plenty in the land will no longer be noticed because of the famine that follows, because the famine will be very severe.
And Pharaoh's dream was repeated a second time, twice, so that the word from God may be true, and God will hasten to do this.
So now look for a wise man of understanding and set him over all the land of Egypt.
Let Pharaoh do this: let him appoint local governors over the land, and take a fifth of everything from all the land of Egypt during these seven years of plenty.
And let them gather all the food of these seven good years that are coming, and let them gather wheat under the hand of Pharaoh. Let the food be stored in the cities.
And let the food be stored for the land for the seven years of famine that will come upon the land of Egypt, so that the land will not be destroyed by the famine.
These words pleased Pharaoh and all his servants.
And Pharaoh said to all his servants: "Where can we find another man like this, in whom is the Spirit of God?"
Pharaoh said to Joseph: "Since God has shown you all this, there is no man wiser or more understanding than you.
You shall be over my house, and my people shall obey your word. Only by the throne shall I be greater than you.
And behold, from this day I have set you over all the land of Egypt."
And Pharaoh took the ring off his own hand and put it on Joseph's hand, and clothed him in a garment of fine linen, and they put a gold chain around his neck.
And he had him ride in the chariot that came after his own, and a herald called out before him, and he set him over all the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh said to Joseph: "I am Pharaoh, and I tell you: without you no one shall lift his hand in all the land of Egypt."
And Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Psonthomphanech, and he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of the City of the Sun, as his wife.
Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians. Joseph went out from Pharaoh's presence and went through all Egypt.
And in the seven years of plenty the land produced fruit.

And during the seven years of plenty he gathered the food, the produce that was in all the land of Egypt, and he placed the food in the cities: the food of the fields around each city he placed in that city.
And Joseph gathered wheat like the sand of the sea, very much, until he could no longer count it, for it was beyond number.
Before the seven years of famine came, two sons were born to Joseph, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of the City of the Sun, bore to him.
And Joseph named his firstborn Manasseh, and said: "God has made me forget all my suffering and everything of my father's house."
And he named the second Ephraim, and said: "For God has made me increase in my humiliation."
The seven years of plenty that had been in the land of Egypt passed,

and the seven years of famine began to come. And there was famine in every land, but in the land of Egypt there was [no lack of] bread. [?: the text literally reads "in the land of Egypt there was no bread"]
And all the land of Egypt grew hungry, and all the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread. Pharaoh said to the Egyptians: "Go to Joseph, and whatever he tells you, do that."
And the famine was over the face of all the land. Joseph opened all the storehouses of wheat and sold to all the Egyptians.
And the whole world came to Egypt [?]
[?] of Pharaoh, that you are spies."
And he put them in prison for three days.
And on the third day he said to them: "Do this and you will live, for I fear God.
If you are peaceable men, I will keep one of your brothers in prison, but you go and take away the grain you have bought.
And bring your brother here to me. Only then will it be seen whether your words are trustworthy; if not, you will die." And they did so.

Each man said to his brother: "Yes, we are in sin because of our brother, for we ignored the anguish of his soul when he begged us, and we did not listen to him. That is why all this trouble has come upon us."
Reuben answered and said to them: "Did I not speak to you and tell you, 'Do not harm this brother of ours'? But you did not listen to me, and now, see, his blood is being demanded."
But they did not know that Joseph understood all of it, for an interpreter stood between them.
And Joseph turned away from them and wept. Then he came back to them and spoke to them in the same way [?]. And he seized Simeon and bound him before their eyes.
And Joseph ordered that their vessels be filled with grain, that each man's silver be put into his sack, and that they be given provisions for the journey. And this was done for them.
And they loaded the grain on their donkeys and left that place.
One of them opened his load to give fodder to the donkeys at the lodging place, and he saw his bundle of silver, for it lay at the top of his sack.

He said to his brothers: "My silver has been given back to me, and here it is in my bag." Their hearts were startled, and they turned to one another in alarm and said: "What is this that the Lord has done to us?"
And they came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan, and told him everything that had happened to them, saying:
"The man who is lord of that land spoke harshly to us and put us in prison as spies of the land.
But we said to him: 'We are peaceable men and not spies.
We were twelve, the sons of one father. One is no longer among us, and the other one is with our father in the land of Canaan.'
The man who is lord of that land said to us: 'By this I will know whether you are peaceable men: leave one of your brothers with me, take the provisions you have bought to your household, and go.
And bring your youngest brother to me, and I will know that you are not spies but peaceable men. Then I will give this brother of yours back to you, and you may move about in this land and trade.'"
As they were emptying their sacks, each man's bundle of silver was found in his sack. When they and their father saw the bundles of silver, they were afraid.
And Jacob their father said: "You have made me childless. Joseph is gone, and now you would take Benjamin as well. All of this has fallen on me!"
Reuben answered his father and said to him: "Let these two sons of mine die if I do not bring him back to you. Put him in my hands, and I will bring him back to you."
Jacob said to him: "My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead and he alone is left. [?] and you would bring my old age down to hell in sorrow."
And the famine grew severe in the land.
When they had finished eating the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them: "Go again and buy us a little food."
Judah said to him, "The man solemnly warned us and said, 'You shall not see my face unless your youngest brother is with you.'
If you send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
If you do not send our brother with us, we will not go down, for the man spoke to us and said, 'You shall not see my face unless your youngest brother is with you.'"
Israel said to them, "Why have you done me this harm? Why did you tell the man that you have a brother?"

But they said, "The man questioned us closely about our family and said, 'Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother?' And we answered him according to his questions. How could we have known that he would say to us, 'Bring your brother'?"
Judah said to him, "Send the boy with me, and let us get up and go, so that we may live and not die, both we and you and our household.
I take responsibility for him; require him from my hands. If I do not bring him back and set him before you, let me bear the blame before you all my days!
If we had not delayed, we would by now have returned three times."

Their father Israel said to them, "Since it is so, do this: take some of the produce of this land in your vessels and carry a gift down to the man: resin and honey, incense and stacte, terebinth nuts and walnuts.
And take double the silver in your hands, and take back with you the silver that was returned in your sacks; perhaps it was some oversight.
And take your brother; get up and go to the man.
And may my God give you favor before the man, and may he send back your other brother and Benjamin. For I am left all alone and bereaved of children."
The men took the gift, and they took double the silver with them, and Benjamin; and they got up and went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.

When Joseph saw them, and Benjamin, his own brother by the same mother, he said to the steward of his house, "Bring these men into the house, and slaughter animals and prepare a meal, so that these men may eat bread with me at noon."
And the man did as Joseph commanded him, and brought the men into Joseph's house.

When they saw that he had brought them into Joseph's house, they said, "It is because of the silver that was found in our sacks the first time that we are being brought in, so that he may falsely accuse us, lay guilt on us, and take us as slaves, along with our [?]."
They came up to the man who was over Joseph's house, at the doors of the house,
and said to him, "We beg you, sir: we came down the first time to buy food;
and when we came to the lodging place and opened our sacks, each man's silver was found in his sack. We have now brought our silver back in our hands, by weight.
And we have brought other silver to buy food. We do not know who put the silver in our sacks."

But he said to them, "Peace be with you; do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your fathers gave you treasure in your sacks. As for me, I received your silver, tested and approved." And he brought Simeon out to them.
And he brought water to wash their feet, and gave fodder to their donkeys.
And they got the gift ready for Joseph's arrival at noon, for they had heard that he would dine there.
Joseph came into his house, and they brought him the gifts they had in their hands, and they bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.
Joseph questioned them and said to them: "Is your aged father well? Is he alive?"
They said to him: "Your servant, our father, is well; he is alive." Joseph said: "Blessed be that man by God!" And they bowed and paid homage to him.
Joseph lifted up his eyes and saw Benjamin, his mother's son, and said: "Is this your youngest brother, whom you said you would bring to me?" And they said to him: "This is he."
Joseph was deeply moved, for his heart yearned over his brother, and he was about to weep. He went into the inner chamber and wept there.
Then he washed his face, restrained his weeping, and ordered the meal to be set out.

They set a place for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because the Egyptians cannot eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
They were seated before him, the eldest according to his seniority and the youngest according to his youth. The men marvelled, each looking at his brother.
Each man received portions from him for himself, but Benjamin's portion was made much larger than theirs. And they drank wine and became drunk with him.
Joseph commanded the steward of his house, saying: "Fill these men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man's silver in the mouth of his sack,
"and put the silver cup in the sack of the youngest, together with the price of his grain." And they did according to Joseph's word, as he had commanded them.
When the night gave way to morning, the men were sent off, they and their donkeys.

When they had gone out of the city and had not yet gone far off, Joseph said to the steward of his house: "Get up, pursue those men, overtake them and say to them: 'Why have you repaid me evil for good? Why have you stolen my silver cup?
"'Is this not the one from which my lord drinks, and with which he practices divination? You have done evil in what you have done.'"
He overtook them and spoke to them according to these words.
They answered and said to him: "Why does our lord speak such words? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing!
"Since we, your servants, brought back to you from the land of Canaan the silver that we found in our sacks, how would we steal gold or silver from your lord's house?
"Whichever of your servants the cup is found with, let him die, and let us become our lord's slaves!"
"But you shall be blameless."
They hurried, and each man took down his load, and each one opened his sack.
He began searching, from the eldest down to the youngest, and found the cup in Benjamin's load.
Then they tore their clothes, and each man loaded his burden onto his donkey, and they returned to the city.
Judah and his brothers came in to Joseph, while Joseph was still in his house, and they fell before him to the ground.
Joseph said to them: "What is this deed you have done? Did you not know that a man such as I practices divination?"

Judah said to him: "What answer shall we give our lord? What shall we say, or how shall we justify ourselves? For God has found out his servants in sin. Here we are, the slaves of our lord, both we and the one with whom the cup was found."
Joseph said to them: "Far be it from me to act according to that word! The man with whom the cup was found, he shall be my slave; but you go up alive to your father."
Then Judah came near to him and said: "I beseech you, lord. Let your servant speak before you, and do not be angry with your servant, for you are next after Pharaoh.
Lord, you asked your servants and said: 'Have you a father or a brother?'
And we said to our lord: 'We have an aged father, and a son of his old age, our brother. His brother died, and he alone is left to his mother, and his father loves him.'
But you said to your servants: 'Bring him to me, and I will take care of him.'
And we said to our lord: 'The boy cannot leave his father; if he leaves his father, he will die.'
But you said to your servants: 'Unless your youngest brother comes, you shall not see my face again.'
And it came to pass, when we went up to your servant, our father, we told him the words of our lord.
And your servant, our father, said to us: 'Go and buy us a little food.'
But we said: 'We cannot go down. But if you send our youngest brother down with us, we will go down, for we cannot see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us.'
Our father, your servant, said to us: 'You know that my wife bore me two sons;
and one of them was lost when he went away from me, and you said: "A wild beast devoured him," and I have not seen him since.
Now if you take this one too from my presence, and sickness befalls him on the way, will you bring down my old age with sorrow to Hades?'
And now, if we go up to your servant, our father, and the boy is not with us (for his soul is bound up with the boy's soul),
then it will be, when he sees that the boy is not with us, that he will die, and we your servants will bring down the old age of your servant, our father, with sorrow to Hades.
For your servant became surety for the boy to his father, and I said: 'If I do not bring him back and set him before you, I shall be guilty before my father all my days.'
Now let me remain as your slave in place of this boy, a household servant of my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers to his father.
If our youngest brother is not with us, I cannot go up to my father either, lest I see the evil that would befall my father."

And Joseph could no longer restrain himself before all those who stood by him, and he said: "Send everyone away from me!" And no one at all stood before Joseph when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
He raised his voice with weeping, and all the Egyptians heard, and it was heard in Pharaoh's house.
Joseph said to his brothers: "I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?" And his brothers could not answer him a word, for they were afraid and were greatly terrified.
Joseph said to his brothers: "Come near to me." And they came near. And he said to them: "I am Joseph, whom you sold into Egypt.
But now do not tremble, and do not let it seem hard to you that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve your life.
For this is now the second year of famine on the earth, and there are yet five more years to come in which there will be neither ploughing nor threshing.
And God sent me ahead of you, so that a remnant of you might remain on the earth, to keep alive on the earth a great remnant.
So now it was not you who sent me here, but God. He has made me like a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
Now hurry to my father and say to him: "This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord over all the land of Egypt. Come down to me and do not delay,
and settle in the land of Goshen, which belongs to Arabia, and be near me, you and your sons and your sons' sons, your sheep and your cattle and everything that is yours,
and I will provide for you there. For there are still five years of famine to come. I will do this so that you and your sons and all your possessions do not perish."
Look, your eyes see, and so do the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my own mouth speaking to you.
Tell my father about all my glory in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring my father here."
Then he threw his arms around the neck of his brother Benjamin and wept over him, and Benjamin wept on Joseph's neck.
He kissed all his brothers and wept with them. After this his brothers talked with him.
The news reached Pharaoh's ears. They told him, "Joseph's brothers have come." Pharaoh was glad, and so were all his servants.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers to do this: 'Fill your sacks with wheat and go to the land of Canaan,
and bring your father and all your possessions and come to me. I will give you the good things of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.'
And you, give your brothers this command: they are to take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and your wives, and you are to bring your father and come.
Do not worry about your belongings, for all the good things of Egypt will be yours."
The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons as King Pharaoh had commanded, and he gave them provisions for the journey.
To each of them he gave two sets of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave two hundred drachmas and five pairs of clothing of various kinds.
He sent gifts to his father in the same way: ten donkeys loaded with all kinds of good things from Egypt, and ten mules carrying bread as provisions for his father's journey.
Then he sent his brothers away and said to them, "Do not get angry with one another on the way."
So they went up from Egypt to the land of Canaan, to their father Jacob,
and told him, "Your son Joseph is alive, and he rules over all the land of Egypt." He was stunned and did not believe them.
They told him everything Joseph had said to them. When Jacob saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of their father Jacob revived,
and Israel said, "It is enough for me if my son Joseph is alive. I will go and see him before I die."
Israel set out with everything he had and came to the Well of the Oath, and he offered sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac.
God spoke to Israel in a vision of the night: "Jacob, Jacob." He answered, "Here I am, Lord."
He said, "I am the God of your fathers. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.
I will go down with you into Egypt, and I will bring you up again in the end, and Joseph will lay his hands on your eyes.
Jacob set out from the Well of the Oath, and the sons of Jacob brought Israel their father. They loaded their belongings and their wives onto the wagons that Joseph had sent.
And they took their produce and all their possessions, everything they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and Jacob went down to Egypt, and his kin with him:
his sons and his sons' sons, and the daughters of his daughters. He brought all his kin down into Egypt.
These are the names of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt with Jacob their father. Jacob and his sons: Jacob's firstborn, Reuben.
The sons of Reuben: Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.
The sons of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin, Ohad and Jachin, Zohar.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
The sons of Judah: Er and Onan in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub and Shimron.
The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon and Jahleel.
These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria, and also Dinah his daughter.
The sons of Gad: Zephon, Haggi and Shuni, Ezbon and Eri and Areli.
The sons of Asher: Imnah and Ishvah, Ishvi and Beriah, and Serah their sister. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter, and who bore these to Jacob: sixteen souls.
The sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife: Joseph and Benjamin.

In Egypt there were the sons of Joseph, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of the City of the Sun, bore to him: Manasseh and Ephraim. There was a son of Manasseh, whom his Syrian concubine bore to him: Machir. And Machir fathered Gilead. The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah and Tahan. The son of Shuthelah: Edem.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher and Ashbel. The sons of Bela were Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh and Muppim. And Gera fathered Ard.
These are the sons of Rachel, whom she bore to Jacob: in all, eighteen souls.
The son of Dan: Hushim.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer and Shillem.
These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter, and she bore them to Jacob: in all, seven souls.
All who entered Egypt with Jacob, those who had come from his loins, not counting the wives of Jacob's sons, were in all sixty-six souls.
The sons of Joseph who were born in Egypt were nine souls. All the souls who entered Egypt with Jacob were seventy-five.
And he sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph, so that Joseph would meet him at the city of Heroonpolis, in the land of Rameses.
Joseph harnessed his chariots and went up to meet Jacob his father at the city of Kateron. He saw him and wept with great weeping.
Israel said to Joseph: "Now I may die from this time on, since I have seen your face, Joseph, and you are still alive."
Joseph said to his brothers: "I will go up and tell Pharaoh. I will say to him: 'My brothers and my father's household, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.'"
"The men are shepherds, for they raise livestock. Their flocks and cattle and everything they have have come."
"If Pharaoh calls you and says to you, 'What is your occupation?'

say: 'We your servants are men who have raised livestock from our youth until now, we and our fathers.' Say this so that we may settle in the land of Goshen, for every shepherd of sheep is an abomination to the Egyptians."
Joseph came and told Pharaoh. He said: "My father and my brothers have come from the land of Canaan, with their flocks and cattle and everything they have, and they are in the land of Goshen."
He brought five men from among his brothers and set them before Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Joseph's brothers: "What is your occupation?" They said: "Your servants are shepherds of sheep,

and we have come to sojourn in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants' flocks, because the famine has grown severe in the land of Canaan. Now let your servants settle in the land of Goshen."

Pharaoh said to Joseph: "Let them dwell in the land of Goshen. If you know that there are capable men among them, appoint them as overseers of my flocks." Jacob and his sons came to Egypt, to Joseph. Pharaoh, king of Egypt, heard of it. Pharaoh said to Joseph: "Your father and your brothers have come to you.
Look, the land of Egypt is before you. Settle your father and your brothers in the best part of the land."
Joseph brought in his father and mother and set them before Pharaoh. Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said: "How many are the years of the days of your life?"

Jacob said to Pharaoh: "The years of the days of my life, during which I have sojourned, are a hundred and thirty years. Few and evil have been the years of the days of my life. They have not reached the days of the years of the life of my fathers, the days during which they sojourned."
Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from him.
Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best part of the land, the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
He measured out grain to his father, his brothers and all his father's household, grain for each person.
There was no grain in all the land, for the famine grew very severe, and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan were exhausted by the famine.

Joseph collected all the silver that was found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan in exchange for the grain that they bought and that he measured out to them. Joseph brought it all into Pharaoh's house.
The silver ran out in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan. All the Egyptians came to Joseph and said to him: "Give us bread! Why should we die before you just because our silver has run out?"
Joseph said to them: "Give me your livestock, and I will give you bread in exchange for your livestock."

They brought their livestock, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for their livestock: for horses and donkeys, for cattle and sheep. And he fed them with bread that year in exchange for all their livestock.

That year ended, and they came to him and said to him: "Let us not be destroyed by our lord. Our silver is spent, and our possessions and livestock have gone to you, our lord. Nothing is left to us before our lord except our bodies and our land.

So that we do not perish before you and the land is not laid waste, buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be slaves to Pharaoh. Give us seed to sow, so that we may live and not perish, and the land [not] be laid waste."
So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh. The Egyptians gave their land to Pharaoh because the famine had overpowered them, and the land became Pharaoh's.
And he made the people servants to Pharaoh, from one end of the borders of Egypt to the other,

except only the land of the priests. That alone Joseph did not buy, because Joseph gave Pharaoh's priests an allowance free of charge, and they ate the allowance that Pharaoh gave them. For this reason they did not sell their land.
Joseph said to all the Egyptians: "Look, from today I have bought you and your land for Pharaoh. Take seed and sow the land.
And of whatever its produce is, give a fifth part to Pharaoh. The other four parts will be your own, as seed for the land and as food for you and all your household."
And they said: "You have saved us. We have found favor before you, our lord, and we will be slaves to Pharaoh."
And Joseph made this an ordinance for the land of Egypt that lasts to this day: a fifth part goes to Pharaoh. Only the land of the priests was excepted; it did not belong to Pharaoh.
Israel settled in the land of Goshen in Egypt and lived there, and they grew and multiplied greatly.
Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the days of his life, the years of Jacob, were one hundred and forty-seven years.

The days of Jacob's death drew near. He called his son Joseph and said to him: "If I have found favor before you, put your hand under my thighs and show me mercy and faithfulness: do not bury me in Egypt.
Bury me with my fathers instead. Carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their tomb." And Joseph said: "I will do so."
Jacob said to him: "Swear to me." And he swore. And Israel bowed down over the top of his staff.
After these things, Joseph was told: "Your father is ill." He took his two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, with him and came to Jacob.
Jacob was told: "Look, your son Joseph has come to you." And Israel gathered his strength and sat up on the bed.
Jacob said to Joseph: "My God appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me,

and said to me: 'I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and make you a nation and a company [of peoples]. I will give this land to you and to your descendants after you as an everlasting possession.'
So now your two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, who were born to you in Egypt, are mine, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
But the children's children who are born to you after these shall bear the name of their brothers; they shall be called after them in their portion.

When I was coming from Mesopotamia of Assyria, Rachel your mother died in the land of Canaan, as I came near the hippodrome in the land of Chabratha, on the way to Ephrathah, and I buried her by the road of the hippodrome, that is, Bethlehem.
When Israel saw Joseph's sons, he said: Who are these?
Joseph said to his father: They are my sons, whom God has given me here. And Jacob said: Bring them here to me, and I will bless them.
Now Jacob's eyes had grown heavy with old age, and he could not see. Joseph brought them near him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
And Israel said to Joseph: Behold, I have not been deprived of your face, and God has shown me your offspring as well.
Joseph brought them out from Jacob's lap, and they bowed down to him on the ground.
Joseph brought his sons: Ephraim with his right hand, toward Israel's left, and Manasseh with his left hand, toward Israel's right, and he brought them near to him.
Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it on Ephraim's head, though he was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh's head, and he crossed his hands.
He blessed them and said: God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac were pleasing, God who has nourished me from my youth until this present day,

the angel who has delivered me from all evil, may he bless these boys! And may my name be called upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they increase into a great multitude upon the earth!
When Joseph saw that his father had laid his right hand on Ephraim's head, it displeased him, and Joseph took hold of his father's hand to lift it from Ephraim's head and lay it on Manasseh's head.
Joseph said to his father: Not so, father, for this one is the firstborn; lay your right hand on his head.

But he would not, and said: I know, my son, I know. This one too shall become a people, and this one too shall be exalted. But his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his offspring shall become a multitude of nations.
And he blessed them on that day and said: By you Israel shall be blessed, and they shall say: May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh! And he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
Jacob said to Joseph: Behold, I am dying, and may God be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers!
I give you Shechem over and above your brothers, which I took from the hands of the Amorites with my sword and my bow.
Jacob called his sons and said: Gather around me, and I will tell you [?] in the last days.
Gather and hear, sons of Jacob, hear Israel your father.
Reuben, my firstborn, the beginning of my children, you were impetuous, impetuous and headstrong.
You boiled over like water. Do not [?], for you went up to your father's bed and defiled the couch you went up on.
Simeon and Levi, brothers, carried out injustice by their [?].
Let my soul not enter into their counsel, and let my liver not join their assembly, for in their anger they killed men, and in their desire they hamstrung a bull.
Cursed be their anger, for their cunning is insolent, for it is harsh. I will divide them among Israel and scatter them among Jacob.
Judah, your brothers shall praise you. Your hands shall be on the backs of your enemies; the sons of your father shall bow down to you.
Judah is a lion's whelp; from the shoot you have come up, my son. Lying down, you shall sleep like a lion and like a lion's whelp. Who will rouse him?
A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his loins, until he comes for whom it is prepared, and he is the expectation of the nations.
He shall tie his foal to the vine, and his donkey's foal to the branch of the vine. He shall wash his garment in wine and his robe in the blood of grapes.
His eyes shall be more joyful than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.
Issachar has desired what is good. He shall rest among his portion,
and he saw his resting place, that it was good, and the land, that it was rich. He gave his shoulders to labor and became a man who tills the land.
Zebulun shall dwell on the seashore, and he shall send out ships, and he shall reach as far as Sidon.
Dan shall judge his people as one tribe in Israel;
and Dan shall be a serpent on the road, sitting in ambush in the paths, and he shall bite the horse's heels, and the rider shall fall backward.
And he waits for the salvation of the Lord.
Gad: a raiding band shall raid him, and he too shall raid it, following on its heels.
Asher: his bread is rich, and he shall provide food for rulers.
Naphtali is a tree, a growing shoot, and he shall give fruit in beauty.
Joseph, my son, grown great, my youngest son, the one to be envied, turn back to me;
against whom they plotted and reviled him, and the masters of the bow were hostile to him.
And their bows were broken by force, and the sinews of the arms of their hands were loosed by the mighty hand of Jacob, who made you strong, Israel; by the God of your father.
And my God will help you and bless you with the blessing of heaven above and with the blessing of the earth, through which all things come to be, for the sake of the blessing of breasts and womb.

By the blessing of your father you have prevailed beyond the blessing of the firm mountains, and as the blessing of the everlasting hills; may they be upon the head of Joseph and upon the crown of him who was leader of his brothers.
Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he shall still be eating, and at evening he shall divide the food.
All these are the sons of Jacob, twelve tribes. This is what their father said to them, and he blessed them; he blessed each one of them according to his own blessing.
And he said to them: "I am being gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the double cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
which is opposite Mamre, in the land of Canaan, the cave that Abraham acquired by purchase from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place.
There they buried Abraham and his wife Sarah, and there they buried Isaac and his wife Rebekah, and there they buried Leah
the purchased field and the cave that is in it, from the sons of Heth.
And Jacob finished giving commands to his sons, and he drew his feet up onto the bed, and he expired and was gathered to his fathers.
And Joseph fell on his father's face, and he wept and kissed him.
And Joseph commanded his servants, the embalmers (literally "those who clothe the dead"), to embalm his father, and the embalmers embalmed Israel.
And they completed his forty days, for that is how the days of burial are counted. And all Egypt mourned him for seventy days.
And when the days of mourning had passed, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh's officials and said to them: "If I have found favour in your sight, speak in Pharaoh's ears and say to him:
'My father made me swear an oath and said to me: "Bury me in the tomb that I made for myself in the land of Canaan." Now therefore let me go up and bury my father, and I will come back again.'"
Pharaoh said to Joseph: "Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear."
And Joseph went up to bury his father. With him went up all Pharaoh's servants, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
and all Joseph's household, all his brothers, and all the kin of his father's house. They left their sheep and cattle in the land of Goshen.
Chariots and horsemen also went up with him, and the company was very great.
And they came to the threshing floors of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and they lamented him there with a very great and loud lamentation. And Joseph mourned for his father for seven days.

And the inhabitants of the land of Canaan saw the mourning at the threshing floors of Atad and said: "This is a great mourning of the Egyptians." For this reason that place, which is by the Jordan, was called "the Mourning of Egypt."
And the sons of Israel did for him just as he had commanded them.
And his sons carried him up to the land of Canaan and buried him in the double cave, opposite Mamre, which Abraham had bought as a burial place from the sons of Ephron the Hittite.
After he had buried his father, Joseph returned to Egypt, together with his brothers and all those who had gone up with him to bury his father.
When Joseph's brothers saw that their father had died, they said: "Perhaps Joseph will remember the wrong against us and pay us back in full for all the evil we did to him."
They came to Joseph and said: "Before his death your father made you swear an oath, and he said to you:

'Say this to Joseph: Forgive their falsehoods and their sins, for they did evil to you.' And now, bear with the offence of the servants of your father's God." And Joseph wept at what they said to him.
They came up to him and said: "We are your servants."
Joseph said to them: "Do not be afraid, for I belong to God."
"You planned evil against me, but God planned good for me, so that it would turn out as it is today, and many people would be fed."
And he said to them: "Do not be afraid. I will feed you and your households." And he comforted them and spoke kindly to them (literally "spoke according to their heart").
And Joseph settled in Egypt, together with his brothers and his father's entire household. Joseph lived one hundred and ten years.
And Joseph saw Ephraim's children down to the third generation. And the sons of Machir, son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph's knees.
Joseph spoke to his brothers and said to them: "I am dying. The Lord will surely visit you, and he will bring you out of this land to the land that he swore to our fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob."
And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear an oath, and said to them: "At that visitation, when God visits you, carry my bones up with you."
And Joseph died at the age of one hundred and ten years, and they buried him and laid him in a tomb in Egypt.
